41.     assert forall|i: int, j: int|
42.         0 <= i < addrs.len() && 0 <= j < addrs.len() && i != j implies addrs[i]
43.         != addrs[j] by {
44.         assert(addrs[i] == base + i * ps);
45.         assert(addrs[j] == base + j * ps);
46.         if addrs[i] == addrs[j] {
47.             // From the equal addresses: i * ps == j * ps.
48.             vstd::arithmetic::mul::lemma_mul_is_commutative(i, ps);
49.             vstd::arithmetic::mul::lemma_mul_is_commutative(j, ps);
50.             // ps * (i - j) == ps * i - ps * j == 0.
51.             vstd::arithmetic::mul::lemma_mul_is_distributive_sub(ps, i, j);
52.             assert(ps * (i - j) == 0);
53.             // A nonzero stride times a nonzero difference cannot be zero.
54.             vstd::arithmetic::mul::lemma_mul_nonzero(ps, i - j);

4. //==================================================================================================
5. // Imports
6. //==================================================================================================
7. 
8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
10. include!("manager.spec.rs");
11. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
12. include!("manager.proof.rs");
13. 
14. use crate::{
15.     hal::mem::FrameAddress,
16.     mm::phys::{
17.         frame,
18.         kframe::KernelFrame,
19.         upool::{
20.             Upool,
21.             UserFrame,
22.         },
23.     },
24. };
25. use ::alloc::vec::Vec;
26. use ::arch::mem;
27. use ::core::{
28.     hint::unlikely,
29.     mem::MaybeUninit,
30.     sync::atomic::{
31.         AtomicBool,
32.         Ordering,
33.     },
34. };
35. use ::sys::error::{
36.     Error,
37.     ErrorCode,
38. };
39. 
40. //==================================================================================================
41. // Constants
42. //==================================================================================================
43. 
44. // Use relaxed ordering for all atomic operations to mitigate synchronization overhead. It is safe
45. // to use this ordering semantics because Nanvix is a single-core system, and the kernel runs with
46. // interrupts disabled.
47. const ORDER: Ordering = Ordering::Relaxed;
48. 
49. //==================================================================================================
50. // Global Variables
51. //==================================================================================================
52. 
53. /// Physical memory manager storage.
54. static mut PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER: MaybeUninit<PhysMemoryManager> = MaybeUninit::uninit();
55. 
56. /// Whether the physical memory manager has been initialized.
57. static PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER_INIT: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
58. 
59. //==================================================================================================
60. // Structures
61. //==================================================================================================
62. 
63. ///
64. /// # Description
65. ///
66. /// Physical memory manager.
67. ///
68. #[verus_verify]
69. pub struct PhysMemoryManager {
70.     upool: Upool,
71. }
72. 
73. //==================================================================================================
74. // Implementations
75. //==================================================================================================
76. 
77. impl PhysMemoryManager {
78.     ///
79.     /// # Description
80.     ///
81.     /// Initializes the physical memory manager singleton.
82.     ///
83.     /// # Parameters
84.     ///
85.     /// - `upool`: User page pool.
86.     ///
87.     /// # Errors
88.     ///
89.     /// Returns `InvalidArgument` if the singleton has already been initialized.
90.     ///
91.     // Trusted shim: writes the `static mut` singleton storage and an `AtomicBool`
92.     // lifecycle gate (raw global state Verus cannot model). The manager-singleton
93.     // lifecycle flag is distinct from the frame-allocator lifecycle and has no
94.     // abstract model (the do-not-modify `PhysMemView` only tracks the allocator);
95.     // the contract therefore states the caller-relevant guarantee: the global
96.     // frame allocator stays initialized and well-formed across this call.
97.     #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, allow(verus_impl_method_marker))]
98.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
99.     #[verus_spec(result =>
100.         requires
101.             phys_view().initialized,
102.             phys_view().inv(),
103.         ensures
104.             phys_view().inv(),
105.             phys_view().initialized,
106.     )]
107.     pub(super) fn init(upool: Upool) -> Result<(), Error> {
108.         if unlikely(PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER_INIT.load(ORDER)) {
109.             return Err(Error::new(
110.                 ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
111.                 "physical memory manager already initialized",
112.             ));
113.         }
114. 
115.         // SAFETY: this happens during kernel initialization and no other threads are running.
116.         unsafe { PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER.write(PhysMemoryManager { upool }) };
117.         PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER_INIT.store(true, ORDER);
118.         Ok(())
119.     }
120. 
121.     ///
122.     /// # Description
123.     ///
124.     /// Gets a mutable reference to the physical memory manager.
125.     ///
126.     /// # Panics
127.     ///
128.     /// Panics if the physical memory manager is not initialized.
129.     ///
130.     /// # Safety
131.     ///
132.     /// This function is unsafe because it returns a mutable reference to a global variable.
133.     ///
134.     /// The caller must ensure:
135.     ///
136.     /// - No other `&mut PhysMemoryManager` reference obtained from this function is live at the
137.     ///   same time (i.e., `&mut` references must not overlap). In practice this is guaranteed
138.     ///   because the kernel is single-threaded and runs with interrupts disabled, so no
139.     ///   re-entrant or concurrent call can alias the reference.
140.     ///
141.     pub unsafe fn get_mut<'a>() -> &'a mut PhysMemoryManager {
142.         if unlikely(!PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER_INIT.load(ORDER)) {
143.             panic!("physical memory manager is not initialized");
144.         }
145. 
146.         // SAFETY: the physical memory manager has been initialized, so the value is valid.
147.         PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER.assume_init_mut()
148.     }
149. 
150.     ///
151.     /// # Description
152.     ///
153.     /// Allocates user frames into caller-provided storage.
154.     ///
155.     /// The returned frames are not guaranteed to be physically contiguous.
156.     /// User allocations are gated by the kernel watermark: if fulfilling the request would
157.     /// leave fewer than `KERNEL_WATERMARK` free frames, the allocation is rejected.
158.     ///
159.     /// # Parameters
160.     ///
161.     /// - `count`: Number of frames to allocate.
162.     /// - `frames`: Mutable reference to a pre-allocated vector into which to store those
163.     ///   frames' addresses. It should have sufficient capacity for `count` entries.
164.     ///
165.     /// # Return Values
166.     ///
167.     /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned and `frames` is filled with `count` frames. Upon failure, an
168.     /// error is returned and any frames allocated by this call are dropped by truncating `frames`
169.     /// back to empty.
170.     ///
171.     // Trusted shim: loops over the global frame allocator (`Upool::alloc`) and the
172.     // caller-provided `Vec`, with `error!`-logging and a clear()-on-error rollback
173.     // that Verus cannot body-verify without editing exec code. The contract is
174.     // stated over `phys_view()` and `frames@`: on success exactly `count` frames
175.     // are handed out (each now allocated); on error the vector is emptied
176.     // (all-or-nothing). Frames are not claimed contiguous.
177.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
178.     #[verus_spec(result =>
179.         requires
180.             phys_view().initialized,
181.             phys_view().inv(),
182.             old(frames)@.len() == 0,
183.         ensures
184.             phys_view().inv(),
185.             phys_view().initialized,
186.             match result {
187.                 Ok(()) => {
188.                     &&& final(frames)@.len() == count
189.                     &&& forall|i: int|
190.                         0 <= i < count as int ==>
191.                             #[trigger] phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(final(frames)@[i]@)
192.                     &&& phys_view().frames.free_frames.finite()
193.                     &&& spec_watermark_ok(phys_view().frames, 0)
194.                 },
195.                 Err(_) => final(frames)@.len() == 0,
196.             },
197.     )]
198.     pub fn alloc_many_user_frames(
199.         &mut self,
200.         count: usize,
201.         frames: &mut Vec<UserFrame>,
202.     ) -> Result<(), Error> {
203.         if !frames.is_empty() {
204.             let reason: &str = "frames vector is not empty";
205.             error!("{reason}");
206.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
207.         }
208.         if frames.capacity() < count {
209.             let reason: &str = "frames vector has insufficient capacity";
210.             error!("{reason}");
211.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
212.         }
213. 
214.         // A zero-sized allocation is trivially satisfied.
215.         if count == 0 {
216.             return Ok(());
217.         }
218. 
219.         Self::check_user_watermark(count)?;
220. 
221.         for _ in 0..count {
222.             match self.upool.alloc() {
223.                 Ok(frame) => frames.push(frame),
224.                 Err(error) => {
225.                     frames.clear();
226.                     return Err(error);
227.                 },
228.             }
229.         }
230.         Ok(())
231.     }
232. 
233.     ///
234.     /// # Description
235.     ///
236.     /// Allocates a single user frame, applying the same kernel watermark check as
237.     /// [`Self::alloc_many_user_frames`]. This is the single-frame fast path used on
238.     /// hot paths such as copy-on-write fault resolution, where allocating an
239.     /// intermediate [`Vec`] would be wasteful.
240.     ///
241.     /// # Returns
242.     ///
243.     /// Upon success, a [`UserFrame`] is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned
244.     /// instead.
245.     ///
246.     // Trusted shim: applies the watermark gate then delegates to the global
247.     // `Upool::alloc`. On success the returned frame's physical address is now in
248.     // the allocator's `allocated_frames` and is page-aligned.
249.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
250.     #[verus_spec(result =>
251.         requires
252.             phys_view().initialized,
253.             phys_view().inv(),
254.         ensures
255.             phys_view().inv(),
256.             phys_view().initialized,
257.             match result {
258.                 Ok(frame) => {
259.                     &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
260.                     &&& frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0
261.                     &&& phys_view().frames.free_frames.finite()
262.                     &&& spec_watermark_ok(phys_view().frames, 0)
263.                 },
264.                 Err(_) => true,
265.             },
266.     )]
267.     pub fn alloc_user_frame(&mut self) -> Result<UserFrame, Error> {
268.         Self::check_user_watermark(1)?;
269.         self.upool.alloc()
270.     }
271. 
272.     ///
273.     /// # Description
274.     ///
275.     /// Rejects user allocations of `count` frames that would breach the kernel
276.     /// watermark, i.e. that would drop the number of free frames below
277.     /// [`config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`].
278.     ///
279.     /// # Parameters
280.     ///
281.     /// - `count`: Number of user frames the caller intends to allocate.
282.     ///
283.     /// # Returns
284.     ///
285.     /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
286.     ///
287.     // Trusted shim: reads the global free-frame count and compares it against
288.     // `KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`. Pure gate, no allocator state change. `Ok` exactly
289.     // captures the watermark policy: at least `KERNEL_WATERMARK` frames remain free
290.     // after servicing `count`. `Err` covers both the overflow guard and a breach.
291.     #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, allow(verus_impl_method_marker))]
292.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
293.     #[verus_spec(result =>
294.         requires
295.             phys_view().initialized,
296.             phys_view().inv(),
297.         ensures
298.             phys_view().inv(),
299.             phys_view().initialized,
300.             phys_view().frames.free_frames.finite(),
301.             match result {
302.                 Ok(()) => spec_watermark_ok(phys_view().frames, count as int),
303.                 Err(_) => true,
304.             },
305.     )]
306.     fn check_user_watermark(count: usize) -> Result<(), Error> {
307.         let watermark_threshold: usize = config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK
308.             .checked_add(count)
309.             .ok_or_else(|| {
310.                 let reason: &str = "watermark + count overflow";
311.                 error!("{reason}");
312.                 Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason)
313.             })?;
314.         if frame::free_count() < watermark_threshold {
315.             let reason: &str = "would breach kernel watermark";
316.             error!("{reason}");
317.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::OutOfMemory, reason));
318.         }
319.         Ok(())
320.     }
321. 
322.     ///
323.     /// # Description
324.     ///
325.     /// Allocates a kernel frame.
326.     ///
327.     /// Kernel allocations bypass the watermark — no artificial ceiling.
328.     ///
329.     /// # Return Values
330.     ///
331.     /// Upon success, a kernel frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
332.     ///
333.     // Trusted shim: allocates one frame from the global allocator (bypassing the
334.     // watermark) and wraps it, freeing the raw frame if wrapping fails. On success
335.     // the returned frame's base address is now allocated and page-aligned.
336.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
337.     #[verus_spec(result =>
338.         requires
339.             phys_view().initialized,
340.             phys_view().inv(),
341.         ensures
342.             phys_view().inv(),
343.             phys_view().initialized,
344.             match result {
345.                 Ok(frame) => {
346.                     &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
347.                     &&& frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0
348.                 },
349.                 Err(_) => true,
350.             },
351.     )]
352.     pub fn alloc_kernel_frame(&mut self) -> Result<KernelFrame, Error> {
353.         let frame_addr: FrameAddress = frame::alloc()?;
354.         KernelFrame::new(frame_addr).inspect_err(|e| {
355.             warn!("failed to wrap frame after KernelFrame::new failure: {e:?}");
356.             if let Err(free_err) = frame::free(frame_addr) {
357.                 warn!("failed to free frame after KernelFrame::new failure: {free_err:?}");
358.             }
359.         })
360.     }
361. 
362.     ///
363.     /// # Description
364.     ///
365.     /// Allocates a contiguous range of kernel frames into caller-provided storage.
366.     ///
367.     /// Kernel stacks require physically contiguous frames because the kernel uses identity
368.     /// mapping and the hardware stack pointer traverses the region linearly.
369.     /// Kernel allocations bypass the watermark — no artificial ceiling.
370.     ///
371.     /// # Parameters
372.     ///
373.     /// - `count`: Number of frames to allocate.
374.     /// - `frames`: Mutable reference to a pre-allocated vector into which to store
375.     ///   those frames' addresses.
376.     ///
377.     /// # Return Values
378.     ///
379.     /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned and `frames` is filled with `count`
380.     /// contiguous entries. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
381.     ///
382.     // Trusted shim: allocates a physically-contiguous run from the global allocator
383.     // (bypassing the watermark) and wraps each frame, with a two-phase
384.     // (`Vec::clear` + `frame::free`) rollback Verus cannot body-verify without
385.     // editing exec code. On success exactly `count` frames are handed out, each now
386.     // allocated, and their base addresses form an ascending page-stride run
387.     // (contiguity is load-bearing for kernel stacks). On error the vector is emptied.
388.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
389.     #[verus_spec(result =>
390.         requires
391.             phys_view().initialized,
392.             phys_view().inv(),
393.             old(frames)@.len() == 0,
394.         ensures
395.             phys_view().inv(),
396.             phys_view().initialized,
397.             match result {
398.                 Ok(()) => {
399.                     &&& final(frames)@.len() == count
400.                     &&& forall|i: int|
401.                         0 <= i < count as int ==>
402.                             #[trigger] phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(final(frames)@[i]@)
403.                     &&& exists|base: int|
404.                         #[trigger] kernel_frames_contiguous(final(frames)@, base)
405.                 },
406.                 Err(_) => final(frames)@.len() == 0,
407.             },
408.     )]
409.     pub fn alloc_many_kernel_frames(
410.         &mut self,
411.         count: usize,
412.         frames: &mut Vec<KernelFrame>,
413.     ) -> Result<(), Error> {
414.         // Check if caller-provided vector is not empty.
415.         if !frames.is_empty() {
416.             let reason: &str = "frames vector is not empty";
417.             error!("{reason}");
418.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
419.         }
420.         if frames.capacity() < count {
421.             let reason: &str = "frames vector has insufficient capacity";
422.             error!("{reason}");
423.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
424.         }
425. 
426.         let base_addr: FrameAddress = frame::alloc_contiguous(count)?;
427.         let base_raw: usize = base_addr.into_raw_value();
428.         for i in 0..count {
429.             let raw_addr: usize = base_raw + i * mem::PAGE_SIZE;
430.             match FrameAddress::from_raw_value(raw_addr).and_then(KernelFrame::new) {
431.                 Ok(kf) => frames.push(kf),
432.                 Err(e) => {
433.                     // Drop already-wrapped frames (frees them via KernelFrame::Drop).
434.                     frames.clear();
435.                     // Free remaining un-wrapped frames from the contiguous allocation.
436.                     for j in i..count {
437.                         let leak_raw: usize = base_raw + j * mem::PAGE_SIZE;
438.                         if let Ok(fa) = FrameAddress::from_raw_value(leak_raw) {
439.                             if let Err(e) = frame::free(fa) {
440.                                 warn!("failed to free leaked frame {fa:?}: {e:?}");
441.                             }
442.                         }
443.                     }
444.                     return Err(e);
445.                 },
446.             }
447.         }
448.         Ok(())
449.     }
450. }

4. // PhysMemoryManager - Specifications
5. //
6. // `PhysMemoryManager` is a *stateless* facade over the global frame allocator
7. // (`Upool` carries no fields; kernel frames are drawn directly from `frame::*`).
8. // It therefore has no per-instance abstract state of its own: the caller-relevant
9. // state is the global frame-reservation state, modelled by the do-not-modify
10. // `phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView` in `mod.spec.rs`. All manager contracts are
11. // stated over `phys_view()` and the returned frame values -- exactly the monotone
12. // style used by the `frame::*` free-function shims (`book`, `alloc_range`, ...).
13. //
14. // See `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-phys-manager/view_design.md` for why a bespoke
15. // `self@` View is *not* realizable here (a constant view cannot witness global
16. // mutation, and there is no `old(phys_view())`).
17. 
18. verus! {
19. 
20. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
21. use crate::mm::phys::{
22.     phys_view,
23.     FrameAllocView,
24. };
25. use vstd::seq::Seq;
26. 
27. /// The kernel watermark threshold, lifted to `int`.
28. ///
29. /// Abstract (uninterpreted) form of the build-time constant
30. /// `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`: the number of physical frames the
31. /// allocator must keep in reserve for kernel use, below which user allocations
32. /// are refused. It is left opaque because the concrete value is a build-time
33. /// constant of an external crate; callers only rely on its consistency, not its
34. /// magnitude.
35. pub uninterp spec fn spec_kernel_watermark() -> int;
36. 
37. /// A user allocation of `count` frames is admissible only if, after servicing it,
38. /// at least `KERNEL_WATERMARK` frames would still be free.
39. ///
40. /// Stated on the abstract free-set cardinality -- never on an allocator counter --
41. /// so it survives any frame-allocator reimplementation. `free_frames.len()` is
42. /// meaningful because the allocator keeps `free_frames` finite (see the shim
43. /// contracts, which (re)establish `phys_view().frames.free_frames.finite()`).
44. pub open spec fn spec_watermark_ok(v: FrameAllocView, count: int) -> bool {
45.     v.free_frames.len() >= spec_kernel_watermark() + count
46. }
47. 
48. /// `addrs` is an ascending, page-stride-contiguous run of frame addresses based
49. /// at `base`: `addrs[i] == base + i * PAGE_SIZE`.
50. ///
51. /// Used to state the contiguity guarantee of `alloc_many_kernel_frames` over the
52. /// sequence of returned kernel-frame addresses (kernel stacks require a linear,
53. /// identity-mapped physical region).
54. pub open spec fn is_contiguous_run(addrs: Seq<int>, base: int) -> bool {
55.     forall|i: int|
56.         0 <= i < addrs.len() ==> #[trigger] addrs[i] == base + i * spec_page_size()
57. }
58. 
59. /// `frames` is an ascending, page-stride-contiguous run of kernel frames based at
60. /// `base`: the address of the `i`-th frame is `base + i * PAGE_SIZE`.
61. ///
62. /// Phrased directly over the `KernelFrame` sequence (using each frame's abstract
63. /// address `@`) so that the `alloc_many_kernel_frames` contiguity guarantee can be
64. /// triggered without an inline closure (closures are forbidden inside triggers).
65. pub open spec fn kernel_frames_contiguous(frames: Seq<KernelFrame>, base: int) -> bool {
66.     forall|i: int|
67.         0 <= i < frames.len() ==> #[trigger] frames[i]@ == base + i * spec_page_size()
68. }
69. 
70. } // verus!
71.

4. // PhysMemoryManager - Proofs
5. //
6. // Abstract laws backing the caller-facing guarantees of the `PhysMemoryManager`
7. // shim contracts in `manager.rs` (stated over `phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView`).
8. // Bodies are discharged here in the proving phase (no `admit()`/`assume()`).
9. 
10. verus! {
11. 
12. /// The many-frame watermark gate subsumes the single-frame one: if servicing
13. /// `count >= 1` frames still respects the watermark, then so does servicing one.
14. ///
15. /// Justifies that `alloc_user_frame` (count = 1) and `alloc_many_user_frames`
16. /// (count) share the same `check_user_watermark` policy.
17. pub proof fn lemma_watermark_monotone(v: FrameAllocView, count: int)
18.     requires
19.         count >= 1,
20.         spec_watermark_ok(v, count),
21.     ensures
22.         spec_watermark_ok(v, 1),
23. {
24. }
25. 
26. /// A contiguous run with a positive page stride has pairwise-distinct addresses:
27. /// distinct indices map to distinct frame addresses.
28. ///
29. /// Backs the "no double-allocation" reading of the contiguity guarantee in
30. /// `alloc_many_kernel_frames`: the `count` returned frames are genuinely distinct
31. /// physical frames, not aliases.
32. pub proof fn lemma_contiguous_run_distinct(addrs: Seq<int>, base: int)
33.     requires
34.         spec_page_size() > 0,
35.         is_contiguous_run(addrs, base),
36.     ensures
37.         forall|i: int, j: int|
38.             0 <= i < addrs.len() && 0 <= j < addrs.len() && i != j ==> addrs[i] != addrs[j],
39. {
40.     let ps = spec_page_size();
41.     assert forall|i: int, j: int|
42.         0 <= i < addrs.len() && 0 <= j < addrs.len() && i != j implies addrs[i]
43.         != addrs[j] by {
44.         assert(addrs[i] == base + i * ps);
45.         assert(addrs[j] == base + j * ps);
46.         if addrs[i] == addrs[j] {
47.             // From the equal addresses: i * ps == j * ps.
48.             vstd::arithmetic::mul::lemma_mul_is_commutative(i, ps);
49.             vstd::arithmetic::mul::lemma_mul_is_commutative(j, ps);
50.             // ps * (i - j) == ps * i - ps * j == 0.
51.             vstd::arithmetic::mul::lemma_mul_is_distributive_sub(ps, i, j);
52.             assert(ps * (i - j) == 0);
53.             // A nonzero stride times a nonzero difference cannot be zero.
54.             vstd::arithmetic::mul::lemma_mul_nonzero(ps, i - j);
55.             assert(false);
56.         }
57.     }
58. }
59. 
60. } // verus!

 `PhysMemoryManager` is the kernel's **single global owner of physical RAM frames**. It
 hands out ownership of individual physical frames in two qualities of service: **user
 frames** (refcounted, watermark-gated, possibly non-contiguous, drawn from `Upool`) and
 **kernel frames** (watermark-exempt, single or physically-contiguous runs, drawn
 directly from the `frame` allocator). Callers care only about: *did I get the exact
 frames I asked for, owned cleanly, with the right contiguity/watermark policy — and on
 failure, is the allocator left untouched with nothing leaked?*
 
 ## Key Invariants (caller perspective)
 - **Lifecycle:** usable only after a successful `init`; `init` is one-shot/monotonic
   (second call errors, never clobbers). `get_mut` is valid exactly when initialized.
 - **Ownership / no double-allocation:** each successful allocation yields frames the
   caller exclusively owns; the same physical frame is never handed to two live owners.
   User frames additionally carry refcount semantics for CoW sharing.
 - **All-or-nothing on bulk ops:** `alloc_many_*` either fully succeed (vector holds
   exactly `count`) or fully roll back (vector empty, every interim frame freed). No
   partial states, no leaks.
 - **Policy split:** user allocations are gated by `KERNEL_WATERMARK`
   (`free_count() >= KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`); kernel allocations bypass it entirely.
 - **Contiguity contract:** `alloc_many_kernel_frames` guarantees physical contiguity;
   `alloc_many_user_frames` makes no such promise.
 - **Caller-provided storage discipline:** bulk APIs require an empty, sufficiently
   pre-reserved `Vec`; they validate and reject otherwise (`InvalidArgument`) rather
   than reallocating.
 
 ## Notes for View Design
 - The natural abstract state is already largely present upstream in
   `mm::phys::mod.spec.rs` (`PhysMemView { initialized, frames: FrameAllocView }` with
   `allocated_frames` / `free_frames` / `refcounts`, plus `phys_view()`). These are
   **do-not-modify** existing definitions and form the obvious anchor:
   - `init`'s post-state ↔ `initialized` flips on (`spec_initialize`).
   - `alloc_*` move frames `free → allocated` (refcount → 1) — analogous to
     `spec_book_frame` / `spec_book_frames`, but driven by allocation rather than
     booking.
   - the watermark gate is expressible against `free_frames` cardinality vs.
     `KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`.
 - The View must NOT expose `Upool` internals, `MaybeUninit`/`AtomicBool` storage, or
   the loop/cleanup mechanics — no caller observes them. Stick to: initialized flag,
   free/allocated frame sets, refcounts, and the contiguity/watermark policy.

105.         // disjointness, allocated <-> positive-refcount consistency, free
106.         // frames have no refcount, refcounts in 1..=255.
107.         &&& self@.wf()

109.         // free_frames.len(). (Set::len is only meaningful on finite sets.)

127. 
128. `FrameAllocView` is frozen, so manager-scoped helpers are declared as free
129. `spec fn`s in `manager.spec.rs` (they *consume/produce* `FrameAllocView`; they do
130. not extend its definition). These are the vocabulary the six target functions'
131. `requires`/`ensures` will be written in.

133. ### Allocation = move free → allocated, refcount 1
134. 
135. The caller-observable effect of *every* successful single-frame allocation
136. (user or kernel) is identical: one frame leaves `free_frames`, enters
137. `allocated_frames`, gains refcount `1`. (Watermark is a *gate*, not part of the
138. post-state; contiguity is a property of the returned addresses, below.)

141. /// Post-state of allocating one previously-free frame `addr`.
142. pub open spec fn spec_alloc_frame(v: FrameAllocView, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
143.     FrameAllocView {
144.         allocated_frames: v.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
145.         free_frames:      v.free_frames.remove(addr),
146.         refcounts:        v.refcounts.insert(addr, 1int),

151. /// each with refcount 1. (Bulk user/kernel allocation.)
152. pub open spec fn spec_alloc_frames(v: FrameAllocView, fs: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
153.     FrameAllocView {

155.         free_frames:      v.free_frames.difference(fs),
156.         refcounts:        v.refcounts.union_prefer_right(

175. /// on any allocator counter.
176. pub open spec fn spec_watermark_ok(v: FrameAllocView, count: int) -> bool {
177.     v.free_frames.len() >= (config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK as int) + count

193. the observable address accessors (`KernelFrame::base()`, `UserFrame::address()`),

198. pub open spec fn is_contiguous_run(addrs: Seq<int>, base: int) -> bool {

227. 
228. | Element | Why needed | Substitution test ("rewrite with a different algorithm?") |
229. |---|---|---|
230. | `allocated_frames: Set<int>` | Callers must know a successful alloc yields a frame *not already owned* (no double-allocation); bulk/contiguity contracts name the moved set. | ✅ Any frame allocator — bitmap, free-list, buddy — has a notion of "currently handed-out frames." Survives. |
231. | `free_frames: Set<int>` | Source of new allocations; the watermark policy is stated over its cardinality. | ✅ Every allocator distinguishes available capacity; representation-independent. Survives. |
232. | `refcounts: Map<int,int>` | User frames are refcounted for CoW sharing; callers rely on "freshly allocated ⇒ refcount 1" and on the allocated⇔positive-refcount law. | ✅ Refcounting is a *caller-facing* QoS property of user frames, not a storage choice; any impl that supports CoW exposes it. Survives. |
233. | `inv := wf() ∧ finite` | Reuses proven frame-allocator law; finiteness makes `free_frames.len()` (watermark) well-defined. | ✅ Pure properties of the abstract sets/map; independent of allocator internals. |
234. 
235. The transition helpers (`spec_alloc_frame`, `spec_alloc_frames`),
236. `spec_watermark_ok`, and `is_contiguous_run` are all phrased over abstract
237. `Set`/`Seq`/`int` and the public `spec_page_size`/`KERNEL_WATERMARK` constants —
238. each survives a complete reimplementation because each restates *what* the
239. operation guarantees, never *how* it is computed.
240. 
241. ---
242. 
243. ## Quality Review
244. 
245. | Criterion | Result |
246. |---|---|
247. | **Substitution** | ✅ Each field describes state any frame allocator maintains; none mentions `Upool`/bitmap/atomic storage. |
248. | **Caller-only** | ✅ Allocated/free/refcount are precisely what `vmem`/`virt::manager` reason about; no internal bookkeeping exposed. |
249. | **Complete** | ✅ Covers ownership/no-double-alloc (`allocated_frames`), watermark (`free_frames.len()`), CoW (`refcounts`), all-or-nothing (`spec_alloc_frames` + frame condition), contiguity (`is_contiguous_run`), lifecycle (delegated to `phys_view`). |
250. | **Minimal** | ✅ Three fields, each used by ≥1 target's spec; `initialized` deliberately excluded as per-instance-constant. |
251. | **No code-as-spec** | ✅ Transitions are set/map algebra; the loop-and-push and two-phase cleanup mechanics are never modeled. |
252. 
253. ---
254. 
255. ## Rejected Alternatives
256. 
257. 1. **`initialized: bool` on the manager View.** Rejected: `init` is static and
258.    the lifecycle is already modeled by the do-not-modify `PhysMemView` /
259.    `phys_view()`. Holding `&mut PhysMemoryManager` implies initialized, so the
260.    field is a per-instance constant — fails minimality/substitution.
261. 
262. 2. **A bespoke `PhysManagerView` newtype duplicating allocated/free/refcounts.**
263.    Rejected: it would re-derive exactly `FrameAllocView` + `wf`, fragmenting the
264.    `mm::phys` vocabulary and adding proof overhead, with no caller-visible gain.
265. 
266. 3. **Separate `user_frames` vs. `kernel_frames` allocated sets.** Rejected: the
267.    user/kernel distinction is a *policy on the allocation path* (watermark gate,
268.    contiguity guarantee), not a property of a frame once owned. The watermark is
269.    captured by `spec_watermark_ok`; contiguity by `is_contiguous_run`. Splitting
270.    the set would leak an implementation-irrelevant taxonomy and complicate the
271.    "a frame is allocated to exactly one owner" invariant. Fails substitution.
272. 
273. 4. **`free_count: nat` / `watermark` as View fields.** Rejected: `free_count` is
274.    derivable as `free_frames.len()` (redundant); the watermark is a compile-time
275.    constant (`config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`), not state. Modeling either as a
276.    field violates minimality.
277. 
278. 5. **`Upool` / bitmap / `MaybeUninit`+`AtomicBool` storage in the View.**
279.    Rejected outright: no caller observes these; they are exactly the "HOW" the
280.    abstraction must hide. Fails substitution and caller-only.
281. 
282. 6. **A `contiguous: bool` flag in the View.** Rejected: contiguity is a property
283.    of a *specific returned run* at a call site, not a standing property of the
284.    manager's state. It belongs in `alloc_many_kernel_frames`'s `ensures` via
285.    `is_contiguous_run`, not in the View.
286.

 pub open spec fn spec_alloc_frame(v: FrameAllocView, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
     FrameAllocView {
         allocated_frames: v.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
         free_frames:      v.free_frames.remove(addr),
         refcounts:        v.refcounts.insert(addr, 1int),
     }
 }
 
 /// Post-state of allocating a whole set of previously-free frames at once,
 /// each with refcount 1. (Bulk user/kernel allocation.)
 pub open spec fn spec_alloc_frames(v: FrameAllocView, fs: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
     FrameAllocView {
         allocated_frames: v.allocated_frames.union(fs),
         free_frames:      v.free_frames.difference(fs),
         refcounts:        v.refcounts.union_prefer_right(
                               Map::new(|a: int| fs.contains(a), |a: int| 1int)),
     }
 }
 ```
 
 These deliberately mirror the existing `PhysMemView::spec_book_frame` /
 `spec_book_frames` shapes (allocation and booking have the same abstract effect),
 keeping the whole `mm::phys` module in one transition vocabulary. The
 "all-or-nothing" bulk contract is captured by stating the success post-state as
 `spec_alloc_frames(old, fs)` and the error post-state as `self@ == old(self)@`
 (frame condition) — no partial-fill state is expressible, which is exactly the
 caller guarantee.
 
 ### Watermark policy (user path only)
 
 ```rust
 /// User allocations are admissible iff servicing `count` frames still leaves at
 /// least KERNEL_WATERMARK frames free. Stated on the abstract free-set size, not
 /// on any allocator counter.
 pub open spec fn spec_watermark_ok(v: FrameAllocView, count: int) -> bool {
     v.free_frames.len() >= (config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK as int) + count
 }
 ```
 
 - `alloc_user_frame` / `alloc_many_user_frames` succeed only when
   `spec_watermark_ok(self@, count)`; on `!spec_watermark_ok` they fail with
   `OutOfMemory` and leave `self@` unchanged.
 - `check_user_watermark(count)` is exactly the decision procedure for this
   predicate (plus an `InvalidArgument` arm when `KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`
   overflows `usize`); it is the shared private gate, no state effect.
 - `alloc_kernel_frame` / `alloc_many_kernel_frames` are specified **without**
   this predicate — kernel allocations bypass the watermark.
 
 ### Contiguity (kernel bulk path only)
 
 Contiguity is a property of the **returned addresses**, not a View field. Using
 the observable address accessors (`KernelFrame::base()`, `UserFrame::address()`),
 the kernel bulk contract is stated over the returned sequence:
 
 ```rust
 /// `addrs` is an ascending, page-stride contiguous run of length `n`.
 pub open spec fn is_contiguous_run(addrs: Seq<int>, base: int) -> bool {
     forall|i: int| 0 <= i < addrs.len()
         ==> addrs[i] == base + i * spec_page_size()
 }
 ```
 
 - `alloc_many_kernel_frames` ensures the returned frames' base addresses satisfy
   `is_contiguous_run(.., base)` for some `base`, and that this run is precisely
   the set moved free→allocated in `spec_alloc_frames`.
 - `alloc_many_user_frames` makes **no** contiguity claim (its `count` frames are
   just *some* set moved free→allocated) — matching "non-contiguity is explicitly
   fine."
 
 ---
 
 ## Mapping to Verification-Order Targets
 
 | Function | Abstract effect over `self@` |
 |---|---|
 | `init` (static, TCB) | establishes subsystem; stated over `phys_view().spec_initialize(..)`, **not** `self@`. |
 | `alloc_user_frame` | `requires`-able success when `spec_watermark_ok(self@,1)`; `Ok` ⇒ `self@ == spec_alloc_frame(old, a)`, returned `UserFrame.address()@ == a`, `a ∈ old.free_frames`. `Err` ⇒ `self@` unchanged. |
 | `alloc_many_user_frames` | preconds: `frames` empty, `capacity ≥ count`. `Ok` ⇒ `self@ == spec_alloc_frames(old, fs)`, `|fs| == count`, `frames` holds exactly those addrs, watermark held. `Err` ⇒ `frames` empty & `self@` unchanged. |
 | `check_user_watermark` | pure: `Ok` ⇔ `spec_watermark_ok(self@, count)` (no overflow); no effect. |
 | `alloc_kernel_frame` | `Ok` ⇒ `self@ == spec_alloc_frame(old, a)`, returned `KernelFrame.base()@ == a`; **no** watermark gate. `Err` ⇒ unchanged. |
 | `alloc_many_kernel_frames` | `Ok` ⇒ `self@ == spec_alloc_frames(old, fs)`, the addrs form `is_contiguous_run(.., base)`, `|fs| == count`; **no** watermark. `Err` ⇒ `frames` empty & `self@` unchanged. |
 
 ---
 
 ## Design Rationale (per field — substitution test)
 
 | Element | Why needed | Substitution test ("rewrite with a different algorithm?") |
 |---|---|---|
 | `allocated_frames: Set<int>` | Callers must know a successful alloc yields a frame *not already owned* (no double-allocation); bulk/contiguity contracts name the moved set. | ✅ Any frame allocator — bitmap, free-list, buddy — has a notion of "currently handed-out frames." Survives. |
 | `free_frames: Set<int>` | Source of new allocations; the watermark policy is stated over its cardinality. | ✅ Every allocator distinguishes available capacity; representation-independent. Survives. |
 | `refcounts: Map<int,int>` | User frames are refcounted for CoW sharing; callers rely on "freshly allocated ⇒ refcount 1" and on the allocated⇔positive-refcount law. | ✅ Refcounting is a *caller-facing* QoS property of user frames, not a storage choice; any impl that supports CoW exposes it. Survives. |
 | `inv := wf() ∧ finite` | Reuses proven frame-allocator law; finiteness makes `free_frames.len()` (watermark) well-defined. | ✅ Pure properties of the abstract sets/map; independent of allocator internals. |
 
 The transition helpers (`spec_alloc_frame`, `spec_alloc_frames`),
 `spec_watermark_ok`, and `is_contiguous_run` are all phrased over abstract
 `Set`/`Seq`/`int` and the public `spec_page_size`/`KERNEL_WATERMARK` constants —
 each survives a complete reimplementation because each restates *what* the
 operation guarantees, never *how* it is computed.
 
 ---
 
 ## Quality Review
 
 | Criterion | Result |
 |---|---|
 | **Substitution** | ✅ Each field describes state any frame allocator maintains; none mentions `Upool`/bitmap/atomic storage. |
 | **Caller-only** | ✅ Allocated/free/refcount are precisely what `vmem`/`virt::manager` reason about; no internal bookkeeping exposed. |
 | **Complete** | ✅ Covers ownership/no-double-alloc (`allocated_frames`), watermark (`free_frames.len()`), CoW (`refcounts`), all-or-nothing (`spec_alloc_frames` + frame condition), contiguity (`is_contiguous_run`), lifecycle (delegated to `phys_view`). |
 | **Minimal** | ✅ Three fields, each used by ≥1 target's spec; `initialized` deliberately excluded as per-instance-constant. |
 | **No code-as-spec** | ✅ Transitions are set/map algebra; the loop-and-push and two-phase cleanup mechanics are never modeled. |
 
 ---
 
 ## Rejected Alternatives
 
 1. **`initialized: bool` on the manager View.** Rejected: `init` is static and
    the lifecycle is already modeled by the do-not-modify `PhysMemView` /
    `phys_view()`. Holding `&mut PhysMemoryManager` implies initialized, so the
    field is a per-instance constant — fails minimality/substitution.
 
 2. **A bespoke `PhysManagerView` newtype duplicating allocated/free/refcounts.**
    Rejected: it would re-derive exactly `FrameAllocView` + `wf`, fragmenting the
    `mm::phys` vocabulary and adding proof overhead, with no caller-visible gain.
 
 3. **Separate `user_frames` vs. `kernel_frames` allocated sets.** Rejected: the
    user/kernel distinction is a *policy on the allocation path* (watermark gate,
    contiguity guarantee), not a property of a frame once owned. The watermark is
    captured by `spec_watermark_ok`; contiguity by `is_contiguous_run`. Splitting
    the set would leak an implementation-irrelevant taxonomy and complicate the
    "a frame is allocated to exactly one owner" invariant. Fails substitution.
 
 4. **`free_count: nat` / `watermark` as View fields.** Rejected: `free_count` is
    derivable as `free_frames.len()` (redundant); the watermark is a compile-time
    constant (`config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`), not state. Modeling either as a
    field violates minimality.
 
 5. **`Upool` / bitmap / `MaybeUninit`+`AtomicBool` storage in the View.**
    Rejected outright: no caller observes these; they are exactly the "HOW" the
    abstraction must hide. Fails substitution and caller-only.
 
 6. **A `contiguous: bool` flag in the View.** Rejected: contiguity is a property
    of a *specific returned run* at a call site, not a standing property of the
    manager's state. It belongs in `alloc_many_kernel_frames`'s `ensures` via
    `is_contiguous_run`, not in the View.

54.   `PhysMemoryManager::get_mut()` will succeed (not panic) and `alloc_*` operations are

89.   any frames allocated mid-loop are released (via `Vec::clear` → `UserFrame::Drop`).

92.   exceeding the watermark, or filling more/fewer than `count` on success.

135. hands out ownership of individual physical frames in two qualities of service: **user

   `check_user_watermark(1)` helper. Only the "watermarked single owned frame or clean
   error" contract matters.
 
 ### `alloc_many_user_frames(&mut self, count, frames: &mut Vec<UserFrame>) -> Result<(), Error>`
 - **Callers assume (preconditions):** they pass an **empty** `Vec` with **capacity ≥
   count**; both are validated (`InvalidArgument` otherwise). The `virt::manager.rs:611`
   caller pre-sizes `uframes` and, on any error, additionally `clear()`s it.
 - **Callers assume (Ok):** `frames` now holds exactly `count` user frames (not
   guaranteed physically contiguous), all owned by the caller, allocation respected the
   kernel watermark. `count == 0` is a trivial success.
 - **Callers assume (Err):** all-or-nothing — `frames` is truncated back to empty and
   any frames allocated mid-loop are released (via `Vec::clear` → `UserFrame::Drop`).
   No partial fills, no leaks.
 - **Would break callers:** leaving `frames` partially filled on error, leaking frames,
   exceeding the watermark, or filling more/fewer than `count` on success.
 - **Would NOT break callers:** non-contiguity is explicitly fine; the loop-and-push
   strategy and `Upool` internals are opaque.
 
 ### `alloc_kernel_frame(&mut self) -> Result<KernelFrame, Error>`
 - **Callers assume (Ok):** one owned `KernelFrame` backed by a real physical frame,
   **bypassing the watermark** (no artificial ceiling — kernel allocations must always
   be servable when memory exists). Callers wrap it in `KernelPage`, optionally
   `clear()` it (frame is not guaranteed zeroed), and build page directories/tables.
 - **Callers assume (Err):** nothing allocated, no leak; the helper already frees the
   raw frame if `KernelFrame::new` fails. Caller propagates via `?`.
 - **Would break callers:** applying the user watermark to kernel allocations (would
   starve page-table/page-directory allocation under memory pressure), or leaking a
   frame when `KernelFrame::new` fails.
 - **Would NOT break callers:** the alloc→wrap→free-on-wrap-failure mechanics are
   internal; callers only need "owned kernel frame or clean error, no watermark."
 
 ### `alloc_many_kernel_frames(&mut self, count, frames: &mut Vec<KernelFrame>) -> Result<(), Error>`
 - **Callers assume (preconditions):** empty `Vec` with capacity ≥ count (validated,
   `InvalidArgument` otherwise). `alloc_kpages` (`virt::manager.rs:748`) enforces this
   itself before calling.
 - **Callers assume (Ok):** `frames` holds exactly `count` **physically contiguous**
   kernel frames (ascending by `PAGE_SIZE`), watermark bypassed. Contiguity is the
   load-bearing guarantee — kernel stacks rely on a linear identity-mapped region.
 - **Callers assume (Err):** all-or-nothing — `frames` cleared, every frame from the
   contiguous block freed (both already-wrapped via `Drop` and not-yet-wrapped via
   explicit `frame::free`), no leaks.
 - **Would break callers:** non-contiguous frames on success, partial fills, or any
   leak on the error path; applying a watermark.
 - **Would NOT break callers:** the base-address + offset wrapping loop and the
   two-phase cleanup are internal details.
 
 ### `check_user_watermark(count) -> Result<(), Error>` (private)
 - **Internal callers** (`alloc_user_frame`, `alloc_many_user_frames`) assume: `Ok`
   iff `free_count() >= KERNEL_WATERMARK + count` (with `count==0` / overflow handled —
   `KERNEL_WATERMARK + count` overflow yields `InvalidArgument`); `Err(OutOfMemory)`
   when the request would drop free frames below the watermark. It is a pure gate with
   no side effects on allocator state.
 - Not part of any external contract; exists only to share the watermark policy between
   the single- and many-frame user paths.
 
 ## Abstract Resource
 `PhysMemoryManager` is the kernel's **single global owner of physical RAM frames**. It
 hands out ownership of individual physical frames in two qualities of service: **user
 frames** (refcounted, watermark-gated, possibly non-contiguous, drawn from `Upool`) and
 **kernel frames** (watermark-exempt, single or physically-contiguous runs, drawn
 directly from the `frame` allocator). Callers care only about: *did I get the exact
 frames I asked for, owned cleanly, with the right contiguity/watermark policy — and on
 failure, is the allocator left untouched with nothing leaked?*
 
 ## Key Invariants (caller perspective)
 - **Lifecycle:** usable only after a successful `init`; `init` is one-shot/monotonic
   (second call errors, never clobbers). `get_mut` is valid exactly when initialized.
 - **Ownership / no double-allocation:** each successful allocation yields frames the
   caller exclusively owns; the same physical frame is never handed to two live owners.
   User frames additionally carry refcount semantics for CoW sharing.
 - **All-or-nothing on bulk ops:** `alloc_many_*` either fully succeed (vector holds
   exactly `count`) or fully roll back (vector empty, every interim frame freed). No
   partial states, no leaks.
 - **Policy split:** user allocations are gated by `KERNEL_WATERMARK`
   (`free_count() >= KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`); kernel allocations bypass it entirely.
 - **Contiguity contract:** `alloc_many_kernel_frames` guarantees physical contiguity;
   `alloc_many_user_frames` makes no such promise.
 - **Caller-provided storage discipline:** bulk APIs require an empty, sufficiently
   pre-reserved `Vec`; they validate and reject otherwise (`InvalidArgument`) rather
   than reallocating.
 
 ## Notes for View Design
 - The natural abstract state is already largely present upstream in
   `mm::phys::mod.spec.rs` (`PhysMemView { initialized, frames: FrameAllocView }` with
   `allocated_frames` / `free_frames` / `refcounts`, plus `phys_view()`). These are
   **do-not-modify** existing definitions and form the obvious anchor:
   - `init`'s post-state ↔ `initialized` flips on (`spec_initialize`).
   - `alloc_*` move frames `free → allocated` (refcount → 1) — analogous to
     `spec_book_frame` / `spec_book_frames`, but driven by allocation rather than
     booking.
   - the watermark gate is expressible against `free_frames` cardinality vs.
     `KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`.
 - The View must NOT expose `Upool` internals, `MaybeUninit`/`AtomicBool` storage, or
   the loop/cleanup mechanics — no caller observes them. Stick to: initialized flag,
   free/allocated frame sets, refcounts, and the contiguity/watermark policy.

1. # View Design: `mm::phys::manager` (`PhysMemoryManager`)
2. 
3. > **Implementation note (spec phase outcome).** A bespoke `self@` View on
4. > `PhysMemoryManager` was found to be *unrealizable* and is **not** used by the
5. > implemented specs. `PhysMemoryManager { upool: Upool }` and `Upool` carry no
6. > fields — the manager is a **stateless facade** whose entire observable state is
7. > the *global* frame-reservation state behind `static mut PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER` and
8. > the `frame::*` statics. A `view(&self)` over a field-less value is a constant, so
9. > it cannot witness global mutation (`old(self)@ == self@` always), and there is no
10. > `old(phys_view())` handle either. The implemented contracts therefore follow the
11. > established `frame.rs` free-function-shim pattern: every target method is
12. > `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` with a `#[verus_spec]` stated over the
13. > do-not-modify `phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView` plus the returned frame values —
14. > **monotone post-state facts** (e.g. "the returned frame's address is now in
15. > `allocated_frames`", `spec_watermark_ok`, `kernel_frames_contiguous`). The
16. > `FrameAllocView`-based vocabulary below is retained because the *contract content*
17. > (allocated/free sets, watermark, contiguity) is exactly what those `phys_view()`
18. > facts assert; only the *carrier* changed from `self@` to the global `phys_view()`.
19. > See `manager.spec.rs` for the realized helpers and `tcb-allowed.md` for the shim
20. > rationale.
21. 
22. ## Abstract Resource
23. 
24. `PhysMemoryManager` is the kernel's **single global owner of physical RAM
25. frames**. Through a `&mut PhysMemoryManager` (obtained from the `get_mut`
26. singleton accessor) a caller hands out *exclusive ownership* of individual
27. physical frames in two qualities of service:
28. 
29. - **user frames** — refcounted (CoW-shareable), gated by the kernel watermark,
30.   not guaranteed contiguous;
31. - **kernel frames** — watermark-exempt, single or a physically-contiguous run.
32. 
33. The only state a caller reasons about across these operations is: **which
34. physical frame addresses are currently allocated vs. free, and the per-frame
35. reference count.** Callers never observe *how* frames are tracked (`Upool`,
36. bitmap, `MaybeUninit`/`AtomicBool` storage) — only the reservation state and
37. whether their request was honored with the right ownership/contiguity/watermark
38. policy.
39. 
40. ---
41. 
42. ## View Struct
43. 
44. The instance-level abstract state is exactly the global frame-reservation
45. state, which the codebase **already** models with the do-not-modify
46. `FrameAllocView`. The manager therefore reuses it as its `View::V` rather than
47. introducing a parallel type:
48. 
49. ```rust
50. // (existing, do-not-modify — reproduced for reference only)
51. pub struct FrameAllocView {
52.     pub allocated_frames: Set<int>,   // frame addresses currently handed out
53.     pub free_frames:      Set<int>,   // frame addresses still available
54.     pub refcounts:        Map<int,int>, // allocated addr -> refcount (1..=255)
55. }
56. 
57. impl View for PhysMemoryManager {
58.     type V = FrameAllocView;
59. 
60.     // closed: the Upool/global-allocator -> abstract mapping is fixed during
61.     // proving and must not leak to callers.
62.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> FrameAllocView;
63. }
64. ```
65. 
66. `self@` denotes the global frame-reservation state observable through this
67. manager: `allocated_frames` are the frames live owners hold, `free_frames` are
68. those an `alloc_*` call may still draw from, and `refcounts[addr]` is the share
69. count of an allocated user/kernel frame.
70. 
71. ### Why not a bespoke `PhysManagerView`?
72. 
73. Every field a manager-specific view would carry (allocated set, free set,
74. refcounts) is already named, well-formed, and proven against by `FrameAllocView`
75. + `FrameAllocView::wf`, and the upstream notes designate it as the anchor.
76. Reusing it keeps the manager contracts in the same vocabulary as `frame::*` and
77. the subsystem `PhysMemView`, avoids a redundant abstraction, and satisfies
78. **Minimal** (no new fields) and **No code-as-spec**.
79. 
80. ---
81. 
82. ## Lifecycle (`initialized`) is *not* an instance field
83. 
84. `init(upool)` is a **static** constructor for the singleton; it does not take
85. `&mut self`. Its caller-relevant effect — "after `Ok`, the subsystem is
86. initialized; every later `get_mut()`/`alloc_*` is valid" — is a property of the
87. **subsystem**, already modeled by the do-not-modify `PhysMemView { initialized,
88. frames }` and `phys_view()` (`spec_initialize` flips `initialized` on).
89. 
90. A caller that *holds* a `&mut PhysMemoryManager` is, by construction, past
91. `init`; per-instance the flag is a constant `true` and carries no information.
92. By the **substitution + minimality** tests an `initialized` field on the manager
93. View would be dead, so it is excluded. `init` is `external_body` (TCB-allowed via
94. `get_mut`/lifecycle reasoning) and states its post-condition over `phys_view()`,
95. not over `self@`.
96. 
97. ---
98. 
99. ## Well-formedness Invariant
100. 
101. ```rust
102. impl PhysMemoryManager {
103.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
104.         // Frame-allocator well-formedness: page-alignment, allocated/free
105.         // disjointness, allocated <-> positive-refcount consistency, free
106.         // frames have no refcount, refcounts in 1..=255.
107.         &&& self@.wf()
108.         // Cardinalities must be finite so the watermark predicate can speak of
109.         // free_frames.len(). (Set::len is only meaningful on finite sets.)
110.         &&& self@.allocated_frames.finite()
111.         &&& self@.free_frames.finite()
112.     }
113. }
114. ```
115. 
116. `wf()` is reused verbatim from `FrameAllocView::wf` (do-not-modify). The two
117. `finite()` conjuncts are the only abstraction-level additions, and they exist
118. solely because the watermark policy is stated over `free_frames.len()` (below);
119. without finiteness `.len()` is undefined.
120. 
121. `view()` is `closed`, `inv()` is `open` — matching the project rule that the
122. abstraction mapping stays hidden while the invariant is visible to callers.
123. 
124. ---
125. 
126. ## Spec Transition Functions & Policy Predicates
127. 
128. `FrameAllocView` is frozen, so manager-scoped helpers are declared as free
129. `spec fn`s in `manager.spec.rs` (they *consume/produce* `FrameAllocView`; they do
130. not extend its definition). These are the vocabulary the six target functions'
131. `requires`/`ensures` will be written in.
132. 
133. ### Allocation = move free → allocated, refcount 1
134. 
135. The caller-observable effect of *every* successful single-frame allocation
136. (user or kernel) is identical: one frame leaves `free_frames`, enters
137. `allocated_frames`, gains refcount `1`. (Watermark is a *gate*, not part of the
138. post-state; contiguity is a property of the returned addresses, below.)
139. 
140. ```rust
141. /// Post-state of allocating one previously-free frame `addr`.
142. pub open spec fn spec_alloc_frame(v: FrameAllocView, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
143.     FrameAllocView {
144.         allocated_frames: v.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
145.         free_frames:      v.free_frames.remove(addr),
146.         refcounts:        v.refcounts.insert(addr, 1int),
147.     }
148. }
149. 
150. /// Post-state of allocating a whole set of previously-free frames at once,
151. /// each with refcount 1. (Bulk user/kernel allocation.)
152. pub open spec fn spec_alloc_frames(v: FrameAllocView, fs: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
153.     FrameAllocView {
154.         allocated_frames: v.allocated_frames.union(fs),
155.         free_frames:      v.free_frames.difference(fs),
156.         refcounts:        v.refcounts.union_prefer_right(
157.                               Map::new(|a: int| fs.contains(a), |a: int| 1int)),
158.     }
159. }
160. ```
161. 
162. These deliberately mirror the existing `PhysMemView::spec_book_frame` /
163. `spec_book_frames` shapes (allocation and booking have the same abstract effect),
164. keeping the whole `mm::phys` module in one transition vocabulary. The
165. "all-or-nothing" bulk contract is captured by stating the success post-state as
166. `spec_alloc_frames(old, fs)` and the error post-state as `self@ == old(self)@`
167. (frame condition) — no partial-fill state is expressible, which is exactly the
168. caller guarantee.
169. 
170. ### Watermark policy (user path only)
171. 
172. ```rust
173. /// User allocations are admissible iff servicing `count` frames still leaves at
174. /// least KERNEL_WATERMARK frames free. Stated on the abstract free-set size, not
175. /// on any allocator counter.
176. pub open spec fn spec_watermark_ok(v: FrameAllocView, count: int) -> bool {
177.     v.free_frames.len() >= (config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK as int) + count
178. }
179. ```
180. 
181. - `alloc_user_frame` / `alloc_many_user_frames` succeed only when
182.   `spec_watermark_ok(self@, count)`; on `!spec_watermark_ok` they fail with
183.   `OutOfMemory` and leave `self@` unchanged.
184. - `check_user_watermark(count)` is exactly the decision procedure for this
185.   predicate (plus an `InvalidArgument` arm when `KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`
186.   overflows `usize`); it is the shared private gate, no state effect.
187. - `alloc_kernel_frame` / `alloc_many_kernel_frames` are specified **without**
188.   this predicate — kernel allocations bypass the watermark.
189. 
190. ### Contiguity (kernel bulk path only)
191. 
192. Contiguity is a property of the **returned addresses**, not a View field. Using
193. the observable address accessors (`KernelFrame::base()`, `UserFrame::address()`),
194. the kernel bulk contract is stated over the returned sequence:
195. 
196. ```rust
197. /// `addrs` is an ascending, page-stride contiguous run of length `n`.
198. pub open spec fn is_contiguous_run(addrs: Seq<int>, base: int) -> bool {
199.     forall|i: int| 0 <= i < addrs.len()
200.         ==> addrs[i] == base + i * spec_page_size()
201. }
202. ```
203. 
204. - `alloc_many_kernel_frames` ensures the returned frames' base addresses satisfy
205.   `is_contiguous_run(.., base)` for some `base`, and that this run is precisely
206.   the set moved free→allocated in `spec_alloc_frames`.
207. - `alloc_many_user_frames` makes **no** contiguity claim (its `count` frames are
208.   just *some* set moved free→allocated) — matching "non-contiguity is explicitly
209.   fine."
210.

216. |---|---|

218. | `alloc_user_frame` | `requires`-able success when `spec_watermark_ok(self@,1)`; `Ok` ⇒ `self@ == spec_alloc_frame(old, a)`, returned `UserFrame.address()@ == a`, `a ∈ old.free_frames`. `Err` ⇒ `self@` unchanged. |

221. | `alloc_kernel_frame` | `Ok` ⇒ `self@ == spec_alloc_frame(old, a)`, returned `KernelFrame.base()@ == a`; **no** watermark gate. `Err` ⇒ unchanged. |
222. | `alloc_many_kernel_frames` | `Ok` ⇒ `self@ == spec_alloc_frames(old, fs)`, the addrs form `is_contiguous_run(.., base)`, `|fs| == count`; **no** watermark. `Err` ⇒ `frames` empty & `self@` unchanged. |
223. 
224. ---

226. ## Design Rationale (per field — substitution test)
227. 
228. | Element | Why needed | Substitution test ("rewrite with a different algorithm?") |
229. |---|---|---|
230. | `allocated_frames: Set<int>` | Callers must know a successful alloc yields a frame *not already owned* (no double-allocation); bulk/contiguity contracts name the moved set. | ✅ Any frame allocator — bitmap, free-list, buddy — has a notion of "currently handed-out frames." Survives. |
231. | `free_frames: Set<int>` | Source of new allocations; the watermark policy is stated over its cardinality. | ✅ Every allocator distinguishes available capacity; representation-independent. Survives. |
232. | `refcounts: Map<int,int>` | User frames are refcounted for CoW sharing; callers rely on "freshly allocated ⇒ refcount 1" and on the allocated⇔positive-refcount law. | ✅ Refcounting is a *caller-facing* QoS property of user frames, not a storage choice; any impl that supports CoW exposes it. Survives. |
233. | `inv := wf() ∧ finite` | Reuses proven frame-allocator law; finiteness makes `free_frames.len()` (watermark) well-defined. | ✅ Pure properties of the abstract sets/map; independent of allocator internals. |
234. 
235. The transition helpers (`spec_alloc_frame`, `spec_alloc_frames`),
236. `spec_watermark_ok`, and `is_contiguous_run` are all phrased over abstract
237. `Set`/`Seq`/`int` and the public `spec_page_size`/`KERNEL_WATERMARK` constants —
238. each survives a complete reimplementation because each restates *what* the
239. operation guarantees, never *how* it is computed.
240. 
241. ---
242. 
243. ## Quality Review
244. 
245. | Criterion | Result |
246. |---|---|
247. | **Substitution** | ✅ Each field describes state any frame allocator maintains; none mentions `Upool`/bitmap/atomic storage. |
248. | **Caller-only** | ✅ Allocated/free/refcount are precisely what `vmem`/`virt::manager` reason about; no internal bookkeeping exposed. |
249. | **Complete** | ✅ Covers ownership/no-double-alloc (`allocated_frames`), watermark (`free_frames.len()`), CoW (`refcounts`), all-or-nothing (`spec_alloc_frames` + frame condition), contiguity (`is_contiguous_run`), lifecycle (delegated to `phys_view`). |
250. | **Minimal** | ✅ Three fields, each used by ≥1 target's spec; `initialized` deliberately excluded as per-instance-constant. |
251. | **No code-as-spec** | ✅ Transitions are set/map algebra; the loop-and-push and two-phase cleanup mechanics are never modeled. |
252. 
253. ---
254. 
255. ## Rejected Alternatives
256. 
257. 1. **`initialized: bool` on the manager View.** Rejected: `init` is static and
258.    the lifecycle is already modeled by the do-not-modify `PhysMemView` /
259.    `phys_view()`. Holding `&mut PhysMemoryManager` implies initialized, so the
260.    field is a per-instance constant — fails minimality/substitution.
261. 
262. 2. **A bespoke `PhysManagerView` newtype duplicating allocated/free/refcounts.**
263.    Rejected: it would re-derive exactly `FrameAllocView` + `wf`, fragmenting the
264.    `mm::phys` vocabulary and adding proof overhead, with no caller-visible gain.
265. 
266. 3. **Separate `user_frames` vs. `kernel_frames` allocated sets.** Rejected: the
267.    user/kernel distinction is a *policy on the allocation path* (watermark gate,
268.    contiguity guarantee), not a property of a frame once owned. The watermark is
269.    captured by `spec_watermark_ok`; contiguity by `is_contiguous_run`. Splitting
270.    the set would leak an implementation-irrelevant taxonomy and complicate the
271.    "a frame is allocated to exactly one owner" invariant. Fails substitution.
272. 
273. 4. **`free_count: nat` / `watermark` as View fields.** Rejected: `free_count` is
274.    derivable as `free_frames.len()` (redundant); the watermark is a compile-time
275.    constant (`config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`), not state. Modeling either as a
276.    field violates minimality.
277. 
278. 5. **`Upool` / bitmap / `MaybeUninit`+`AtomicBool` storage in the View.**
279.    Rejected outright: no caller observes these; they are exactly the "HOW" the
280.    abstraction must hide. Fails substitution and caller-only.
281. 
282. 6. **A `contiguous: bool` flag in the View.** Rejected: contiguity is a property
283.    of a *specific returned run* at a call site, not a standing property of the
284.    manager's state. It belongs in `alloc_many_kernel_frames`'s `ensures` via
285.    `is_contiguous_run`, not in the View.

 # View Design: `mm::phys::manager` (`PhysMemoryManager`)
 
 > **Implementation note (spec phase outcome).** A bespoke `self@` View on
 > `PhysMemoryManager` was found to be *unrealizable* and is **not** used by the
 > implemented specs. `PhysMemoryManager { upool: Upool }` and `Upool` carry no
 > fields — the manager is a **stateless facade** whose entire observable state is
 > the *global* frame-reservation state behind `static mut PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER` and
 > the `frame::*` statics. A `view(&self)` over a field-less value is a constant, so
 > it cannot witness global mutation (`old(self)@ == self@` always), and there is no
 > `old(phys_view())` handle either. The implemented contracts therefore follow the
 > established `frame.rs` free-function-shim pattern: every target method is
 > `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` with a `#[verus_spec]` stated over the
 > do-not-modify `phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView` plus the returned frame values —
 > **monotone post-state facts** (e.g. "the returned frame's address is now in
 > `allocated_frames`", `spec_watermark_ok`, `kernel_frames_contiguous`). The
 > `FrameAllocView`-based vocabulary below is retained because the *contract content*
 > (allocated/free sets, watermark, contiguity) is exactly what those `phys_view()`
 > facts assert; only the *carrier* changed from `self@` to the global `phys_view()`.
 > See `manager.spec.rs` for the realized helpers and `tcb-allowed.md` for the shim
 > rationale.
 
 ## Abstract Resource
 
 `PhysMemoryManager` is the kernel's **single global owner of physical RAM
 frames**. Through a `&mut PhysMemoryManager` (obtained from the `get_mut`
 singleton accessor) a caller hands out *exclusive ownership* of individual
 physical frames in two qualities of service:
 
 - **user frames** — refcounted (CoW-shareable), gated by the kernel watermark,
   not guaranteed contiguous;
 - **kernel frames** — watermark-exempt, single or a physically-contiguous run.
 
 The only state a caller reasons about across these operations is: **which
 physical frame addresses are currently allocated vs. free, and the per-frame
 reference count.** Callers never observe *how* frames are tracked (`Upool`,
 bitmap, `MaybeUninit`/`AtomicBool` storage) — only the reservation state and
 whether their request was honored with the right ownership/contiguity/watermark
 policy.
 
 ---
 
 ## View Struct
 
 The instance-level abstract state is exactly the global frame-reservation
 state, which the codebase **already** models with the do-not-modify
 `FrameAllocView`. The manager therefore reuses it as its `View::V` rather than
 introducing a parallel type:
 
 ```rust
 // (existing, do-not-modify — reproduced for reference only)
 pub struct FrameAllocView {
     pub allocated_frames: Set<int>,   // frame addresses currently handed out
     pub free_frames:      Set<int>,   // frame addresses still available
     pub refcounts:        Map<int,int>, // allocated addr -> refcount (1..=255)
 }
 
 impl View for PhysMemoryManager {
     type V = FrameAllocView;
 
     // closed: the Upool/global-allocator -> abstract mapping is fixed during
     // proving and must not leak to callers.
     closed spec fn view(&self) -> FrameAllocView;
 }
 ```
 
 `self@` denotes the global frame-reservation state observable through this
 manager: `allocated_frames` are the frames live owners hold, `free_frames` are
 those an `alloc_*` call may still draw from, and `refcounts[addr]` is the share
 count of an allocated user/kernel frame.
 
 ### Why not a bespoke `PhysManagerView`?
 
 Every field a manager-specific view would carry (allocated set, free set,
 refcounts) is already named, well-formed, and proven against by `FrameAllocView`
 + `FrameAllocView::wf`, and the upstream notes designate it as the anchor.
 Reusing it keeps the manager contracts in the same vocabulary as `frame::*` and
 the subsystem `PhysMemView`, avoids a redundant abstraction, and satisfies
 **Minimal** (no new fields) and **No code-as-spec**.
 
 ---
 
 ## Lifecycle (`initialized`) is *not* an instance field
 
 `init(upool)` is a **static** constructor for the singleton; it does not take
 `&mut self`. Its caller-relevant effect — "after `Ok`, the subsystem is
 initialized; every later `get_mut()`/`alloc_*` is valid" — is a property of the
 **subsystem**, already modeled by the do-not-modify `PhysMemView { initialized,
 frames }` and `phys_view()` (`spec_initialize` flips `initialized` on).
 
 A caller that *holds* a `&mut PhysMemoryManager` is, by construction, past
 `init`; per-instance the flag is a constant `true` and carries no information.
 By the **substitution + minimality** tests an `initialized` field on the manager
 View would be dead, so it is excluded. `init` is `external_body` (TCB-allowed via
 `get_mut`/lifecycle reasoning) and states its post-condition over `phys_view()`,
 not over `self@`.
 
 ---
 
 ## Well-formedness Invariant
 
 ```rust
 impl PhysMemoryManager {
     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
         // Frame-allocator well-formedness: page-alignment, allocated/free
         // disjointness, allocated <-> positive-refcount consistency, free
         // frames have no refcount, refcounts in 1..=255.
         &&& self@.wf()
         // Cardinalities must be finite so the watermark predicate can speak of
         // free_frames.len(). (Set::len is only meaningful on finite sets.)
         &&& self@.allocated_frames.finite()
         &&& self@.free_frames.finite()
     }
 }
 ```
 
 `wf()` is reused verbatim from `FrameAllocView::wf` (do-not-modify). The two
 `finite()` conjuncts are the only abstraction-level additions, and they exist
 solely because the watermark policy is stated over `free_frames.len()` (below);
 without finiteness `.len()` is undefined.
 
 `view()` is `closed`, `inv()` is `open` — matching the project rule that the
 abstraction mapping stays hidden while the invariant is visible to callers.
 
 ---
 
 ## Spec Transition Functions & Policy Predicates
 
 `FrameAllocView` is frozen, so manager-scoped helpers are declared as free
 `spec fn`s in `manager.spec.rs` (they *consume/produce* `FrameAllocView`; they do
 not extend its definition). These are the vocabulary the six target functions'
 `requires`/`ensures` will be written in.
 
 ### Allocation = move free → allocated, refcount 1
 
 The caller-observable effect of *every* successful single-frame allocation
 (user or kernel) is identical: one frame leaves `free_frames`, enters
 `allocated_frames`, gains refcount `1`. (Watermark is a *gate*, not part of the
 post-state; contiguity is a property of the returned addresses, below.)
 
 ```rust
 /// Post-state of allocating one previously-free frame `addr`.
 pub open spec fn spec_alloc_frame(v: FrameAllocView, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
     FrameAllocView {
         allocated_frames: v.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
         free_frames:      v.free_frames.remove(addr),
         refcounts:        v.refcounts.insert(addr, 1int),
     }
 }
 
 /// Post-state of allocating a whole set of previously-free frames at once,
 /// each with refcount 1. (Bulk user/kernel allocation.)
 pub open spec fn spec_alloc_frames(v: FrameAllocView, fs: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
     FrameAllocView {
         allocated_frames: v.allocated_frames.union(fs),
         free_frames:      v.free_frames.difference(fs),
         refcounts:        v.refcounts.union_prefer_right(
                               Map::new(|a: int| fs.contains(a), |a: int| 1int)),
     }
 }
 ```
 
 These deliberately mirror the existing `PhysMemView::spec_book_frame` /
 `spec_book_frames` shapes (allocation and booking have the same abstract effect),
 keeping the whole `mm::phys` module in one transition vocabulary. The
 "all-or-nothing" bulk contract is captured by stating the success post-state as
 `spec_alloc_frames(old, fs)` and the error post-state as `self@ == old(self)@`
 (frame condition) — no partial-fill state is expressible, which is exactly the
 caller guarantee.
 
 ### Watermark policy (user path only)
 
 ```rust
 /// User allocations are admissible iff servicing `count` frames still leaves at
 /// least KERNEL_WATERMARK frames free. Stated on the abstract free-set size, not
 /// on any allocator counter.
 pub open spec fn spec_watermark_ok(v: FrameAllocView, count: int) -> bool {
     v.free_frames.len() >= (config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK as int) + count
 }
 ```
 
 - `alloc_user_frame` / `alloc_many_user_frames` succeed only when
   `spec_watermark_ok(self@, count)`; on `!spec_watermark_ok` they fail with
   `OutOfMemory` and leave `self@` unchanged.
 - `check_user_watermark(count)` is exactly the decision procedure for this
   predicate (plus an `InvalidArgument` arm when `KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`
   overflows `usize`); it is the shared private gate, no state effect.
 - `alloc_kernel_frame` / `alloc_many_kernel_frames` are specified **without**
   this predicate — kernel allocations bypass the watermark.
 
 ### Contiguity (kernel bulk path only)
 
 Contiguity is a property of the **returned addresses**, not a View field. Using
 the observable address accessors (`KernelFrame::base()`, `UserFrame::address()`),
 the kernel bulk contract is stated over the returned sequence:
 
 ```rust
 /// `addrs` is an ascending, page-stride contiguous run of length `n`.
 pub open spec fn is_contiguous_run(addrs: Seq<int>, base: int) -> bool {
     forall|i: int| 0 <= i < addrs.len()
         ==> addrs[i] == base + i * spec_page_size()
 }
 ```
 
 - `alloc_many_kernel_frames` ensures the returned frames' base addresses satisfy
   `is_contiguous_run(.., base)` for some `base`, and that this run is precisely
   the set moved free→allocated in `spec_alloc_frames`.
 - `alloc_many_user_frames` makes **no** contiguity claim (its `count` frames are
   just *some* set moved free→allocated) — matching "non-contiguity is explicitly
   fine."

 ## Rejected Alternatives
 
 1. **`initialized: bool` on the manager View.** Rejected: `init` is static and
    the lifecycle is already modeled by the do-not-modify `PhysMemView` /
    `phys_view()`. Holding `&mut PhysMemoryManager` implies initialized, so the
    field is a per-instance constant — fails minimality/substitution.
 
 2. **A bespoke `PhysManagerView` newtype duplicating allocated/free/refcounts.**
    Rejected: it would re-derive exactly `FrameAllocView` + `wf`, fragmenting the
    `mm::phys` vocabulary and adding proof overhead, with no caller-visible gain.
 
 3. **Separate `user_frames` vs. `kernel_frames` allocated sets.** Rejected: the
    user/kernel distinction is a *policy on the allocation path* (watermark gate,
    contiguity guarantee), not a property of a frame once owned. The watermark is
    captured by `spec_watermark_ok`; contiguity by `is_contiguous_run`. Splitting
    the set would leak an implementation-irrelevant taxonomy and complicate the
    "a frame is allocated to exactly one owner" invariant. Fails substitution.
 
 4. **`free_count: nat` / `watermark` as View fields.** Rejected: `free_count` is
    derivable as `free_frames.len()` (redundant); the watermark is a compile-time
    constant (`config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`), not state. Modeling either as a
    field violates minimality.
 
 5. **`Upool` / bitmap / `MaybeUninit`+`AtomicBool` storage in the View.**
    Rejected outright: no caller observes these; they are exactly the "HOW" the
    abstraction must hide. Fails substitution and caller-only.
 
 6. **A `contiguous: bool` flag in the View.** Rejected: contiguity is a property
    of a *specific returned run* at a call site, not a standing property of the
    manager's state. It belongs in `alloc_many_kernel_frames`'s `ensures` via
    `is_contiguous_run`, not in the View.

20. pub struct FrameAllocView

23.     pub free_frames: Set<int>,
24.     /// Maps each allocated frame address to its reference count.
25.     /// A frame is present in the map iff it is currently allocated.
26.     pub refcounts: Map<int, int>,
27. }
28. 
29. impl FrameAllocView

31.     pub open spec fn wf(&self) -> bool
32.     {
33.         // Page-alignment
34.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
35.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
36.         // Disjoint
37.         &&& self.allocated_frames.disjoint(self.free_frames)
38.         // Allocated ↔ refcount consistency: a frame is allocated iff it has a positive refcount
39.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) <==>
40.             self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) && self.refcounts[addr] > 0
41.         // Free frames have no refcount entry
42.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==>
43.             !self.refcounts.contains_key(addr)
44.         // Refcount bounded by u8 range
45.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) ==>

data.deltaContent: an arbitrary fixed integer. But the contracts that use it—like `check_user_watermark`
—are marked `external_body`, which means the connection between the real `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK` and the spec function is never actually verified. It
's trusted implicitly through the external_body annotation. This creates a gap: the spec claims `spec_watermark_ok` means `free_frames.len() >= spec_kernel_
watermark() + count`, but that relationship isn't verified—it's just asserted via the
external function's contract.

data.deltaContent: The
guardrails explicitly ban uninterp spec functions, and `spec_kernel_watermark` isn't in the do-not-modify
list, so this is technically a violation. The doc comment tries to justify it by saying the concrete value is a build-time constant from
an external crate and callers only care about consistency, not magnitude. But that rationale doesn
't override the strict rule. I should flag this as a guardrail concern.
