4. // PhysMemoryManager - Specifications
5. //
6. // This file contains specification functions and view types.
7. 
8. verus! {
9. 
10. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
11. use vstd::map::*;
12. 
13. pub uninterp spec fn byte_at_address(ptr: int) -> u8;
14. 
15. /// Abstract view of the frame allocator (`frame::Inner`).
16. ///
17. /// Captures which physical frames are currently allocated vs. free,
18. /// together with a per-frame reference count that models shared
19. /// ownership (e.g. copy-on-write after `share()`).
20. pub struct FrameAllocView
21. {
22.     pub allocated_frames: Set<int>,
23.     pub free_frames: Set<int>,
24.     /// Maps each allocated frame address to its reference count.
25.     /// A frame is present in the map iff it is currently allocated.
26.     pub refcounts: Map<int, int>,
27. }
28. 
29. impl FrameAllocView
30. {
31.     pub open spec fn wf(&self) -> bool
32.     {
33.         // Page-alignment
34.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
35.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
36.         // Disjoint
37.         &&& self.allocated_frames.disjoint(self.free_frames)
38.         // Allocated ↔ refcount consistency: a frame is allocated iff it has a positive refcount
39.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) <==>
40.             self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) && self.refcounts[addr] > 0
41.         // Free frames have no refcount entry
42.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==>
43.             !self.refcounts.contains_key(addr)
44.         // Refcount bounded by u8 range
45.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) ==>
46.             0 < self.refcounts[addr] <= 255
47.     }
48. }
49. 
50. } // end verus!
51. 
52. //==================================================================================================
53. // std `LinkedList` type specification
54. //==================================================================================================
55. //
56. // vstd does not provide a specification for `alloc::collections::LinkedList`. Verified functions in
57. // this module (`init`) take `LinkedList` parameters, so Verus needs to know the type. We declare it
58. // as an opaque external type. We deliberately do NOT provide a `View`/iterator specification: doing
59. // so requires implementing vstd's `View`/`ForLoopGhostIterator` traits for the foreign std types
60. // `LinkedList`/`Iter`, which the Rust orphan rule forbids from a downstream crate (E0117), and the
61. // pinned `vstd` dependency cannot be extended. Consequently the `for region in list.iter()` loops in
62. // `book_physical_memory_regions` / `book_mmio_regions` cannot be body-verified here; those two
63. // functions are marked `external_body` (see `verus-unsupported.md`).
64. 
65. verus! {
66. 
67. use core::alloc::Allocator;
68. 
69. #[verifier::external_type_specification]
70. #[verifier::external_body]
71. #[verifier::reject_recursive_types(T)]
72. #[verifier::reject_recursive_types(A)]
73. pub struct ExLinkedList<T, A: Allocator>(LinkedList<T, A>);
74. 
75. } // end verus!
76. 
77. //==================================================================================================
78. // `mm::phys` boot-subsystem View
79. //==================================================================================================
80. 
81. verus! {
82. 
83. use vstd::set_lib::set_int_range;
84. 
85. /// Abstract state of the global physical-memory subsystem managed by `mm::phys`.
86. ///
87. /// Models the boot lifecycle of the frame-allocator singleton plus its
88. /// frame-reservation state. The `frames` component mirrors `frame::instance()@`;
89. /// the `initialized` flag mirrors the `INSTANCE_INIT` lifecycle gate.
90. pub struct PhysMemView {
91.     /// Whether the frame-allocator singleton has been established
92.     /// (i.e. `init` ran once and returned `Ok`). Models one-shot/monotonic
93.     /// boot: `false` before `init`, `true` after a successful `init`.
94.     pub initialized: bool,
95.     /// Abstract reservation state of the global frame allocator: which physical
96.     /// frames are reserved (allocated) vs. free, with per-frame refcounts.
97.     /// Meaningful (well-formed) only once `initialized` is `true`.
98.     pub frames: FrameAllocView,
99. }
100. 
101. impl PhysMemView {
102.     /// Well-formedness: once the allocator is established, the frame-allocator
103.     /// invariant holds. Before initialization there is no allocator, so no
104.     /// constraint applies.
105.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
106.         self.initialized ==> self.frames.wf()
107.     }
108. 
109.     /// Frames the allocator actually tracks (covered by the bitmap): the union
110.     /// of reserved and free frames. The abstract form of `is_covered`.
111.     pub open spec fn covered(self) -> Set<int> {
112.         self.frames.allocated_frames.union(self.frames.free_frames)
113.     }
114. 
115.     /// The set of frame addresses occupied by a region `[start, start+size)`.
116.     pub open spec fn region_frames(start: int, size: int) -> Set<int> {
117.         let first = start / spec_page_size();
118.         let last = (start + size) / spec_page_size();
119.         set_int_range(first, last).map(|i: int| i * spec_page_size())
120.     }
121. 
122.     /// `init` established the allocator from the caller-supplied bitmap state;
123.     /// lifecycle flips on.
124.     pub open spec fn spec_initialize(self, initial: FrameAllocView) -> PhysMemView {
125.         PhysMemView { initialized: true, frames: initial }
126.     }
127. 
128.     /// Book one covered frame: move `addr` from free to allocated, refcount = 1.
129.     /// Mirrors `Inner::book`'s `Ok` post-state.
130.     pub open spec fn spec_book_frame(self, addr: int) -> PhysMemView {
131.         PhysMemView {
132.             frames: FrameAllocView {
133.                 allocated_frames: self.frames.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
134.                 free_frames: self.frames.free_frames.remove(addr),
135.                 refcounts: self.frames.refcounts.insert(addr, 1int),
136.             },
137.             ..self
138.         }
139.     }
140. 
141.     /// Book a set of frames at once: move them all from free to allocated, each
142.     /// with refcount = 1. Mirrors `Inner::alloc_range`'s `Ok` post-state and
143.     /// generalizes it from a contiguous region to an arbitrary frame set.
144.     pub open spec fn spec_book_frames(self, frames: Set<int>) -> PhysMemView {
145.         PhysMemView {
146.             frames: FrameAllocView {
147.                 allocated_frames: self.frames.allocated_frames.union(frames),
148.                 free_frames: self.frames.free_frames.difference(frames),
149.                 refcounts: self.frames.refcounts.union_prefer_right(
150.                     Map::new(|a: int| frames.contains(a), |a: int| 1int),
151.                 ),
152.             },
153.             ..self
154.         }
155.     }
156. }
157. 
158. /// Abstract view of the global physical-memory subsystem at the current program
159. /// point.
160. ///
161. /// The subsystem state lives in module-level `static`s (`frame::INSTANCE` /
162. /// `frame::INSTANCE_INIT`) that a Verus `spec fn` cannot read directly, so this
163. /// is an *uninterpreted* function: the exec wrappers in `frame.rs` and the
164. /// `book_*`/`init` functions pin down its value through their `ensures` clauses.
165. /// `initialized` mirrors `INSTANCE_INIT`; `frames` mirrors `frame::instance()@`.
166. ///
167. /// This is the handle the caller-facing contract of `init` is stated over: after
168. /// a successful `init`, `phys_view().initialized` and `phys_view().inv()` hold, so
169. /// every later `frame::*` / `PhysMemoryManager::*` operation may rely on the
170. /// frame-allocator invariant.
171. pub uninterp spec fn phys_view() -> PhysMemView;
172. 
173. } // end verus!

data.deltaContent: I
'm finding three functions with tautological error postconditions — alloc_user_frame, check_
user_watermark, and alloc_kernel_frame all have `Err(_) => true` — which violates strict spec-design principles. The
callers expect guarantees like "nothing allocated, no leak, state unchanged" that aren't captured in the spec. However, there
's a mitigating factor: the unconditional ensures on allocator invariant and initialized state do apply on all paths.
The real issue is that state-preservation can't be expressed given the monotone-no-old carrier design
, whereas the bulk functions managed to express vector rollback. For single-frame functions with
no out-param, the global phys_view has no old() reference
, making `Err(_) => true` the maximum achievable rather than a laziness problem.
I
'm flagging this as a Medium quality weakness — it's a recognized anti-pattern per
the review scope, but defensible given the carrier constraints. The global inv() and initialized ensures provide

partial mitigation, though they don't formally guarantee the caller's "no leak / state unchanged" expectation.

Now looking
at the init contract, which is near-vacuous: it requires initialized and ensures initialized, so the postcondition is trivially maintained

. The actual semantic effect — establishing the manager singleton so get_mut won't panic — isn't captured at all. Callers assume the singleton is now live and every later get_mut will succeed, but the
manager-singleton lifecycle has no abstract model in the spec, making init's contract essentially a frame-preservation no-op.
The
precondition requiring initialized is actually strong and correct — it matches the boot ordering where
frame::init runs before PhysMemoryManager::init — but it means the spec adds nothing beyond "I preserve the already-established allocator." This is a
notable spec-completeness gap, though acceptable since init is external_body and the prec

ondition is satisfiable at the call site. I'll flag this as Medium.

For spec
_kernel_watermark(), it's uninterp with no injecting axioms, modeling an external build-time constant, which creates tension with the "uninterp banned" constraint.
The spec could be more faithful by defining it concretely as the actual KERNEL_WATERMARK constant, but resolving cross-crate constants
in Verus is genuinely difficult, and since check_user_watermark is external_
body anyway, the abstraction is acceptable. I'll flag this as a quality concern but not a hard blocker, since
uninterp isn't in the explicit guardrail blockers list.

data.reasoningText:
Looking at the cfg-gating patterns in manager.rs, the spec and proof modules are properly gated with conditional includes, which is allowed, while the lint attributes are only applied under verus and don't affect semantics, so those are fine too.

Now examining the cheating dimensions across the three manager files: there are 6 external_body calls (all documented in tcb-allowed.md), 1 uninterpreted function (spec_kernel_watermark), and no cfg-gated exec code since the cfg usages are just include-gating and lint attributes. I'm verifying each of the 6 external_body entries against the allowed list to confirm they're all accounted for, then I'll move into the deeper spec-quality analysis and caller coverage before writing the full review.

I'm finding three functions with tautological error postconditions — alloc_user_frame, check_user_watermark, and alloc_kernel_frame all have `Err(_) => true` — which violates strict spec-design principles. The callers expect guarantees like "nothing allocated, no leak, state unchanged" that aren't captured in the spec. However, there's a mitigating factor: the unconditional ensures on allocator invariant and initialized state do apply on all paths. The real issue is that state-preservation can't be expressed given the monotone-no-old carrier design, whereas the bulk functions managed to express vector rollback. For single-frame functions with no out-param, the global phys_view has no old() reference, making `Err(_) => true` the maximum achievable rather than a laziness problem.

I'm flagging this as a Medium quality weakness — it's a recognized anti-pattern per the review scope, but defensible given the carrier constraints. The global inv() and initialized ensures provide partial mitigation, though they don't formally guarantee the caller's "no leak / state unchanged" expectation.

Now looking at the init contract, which is near-vacuous: it requires initialized and ensures initialized, so the postcondition is trivially maintained. The actual semantic effect — establishing the manager singleton so get_mut won't panic — isn't captured at all. Callers assume the singleton is now live and every later get_mut will succeed, but the manager-singleton lifecycle has no abstract model in the spec, making init's contract essentially a frame-preservation no-op.

The precondition requiring initialized is actually strong and correct — it matches the boot ordering where frame::init runs before PhysMemoryManager::init — but it means the spec adds nothing beyond "I preserve the already-established allocator." This is a notable spec-completeness gap, though acceptable since init is external_body and the precondition is satisfiable at the call site. I'll flag this as Medium.

For spec_kernel_watermark(), it's uninterp with no injecting axioms, modeling an external build-time constant, which creates tension with the "uninterp banned" constraint.  The spec could be more faithful by defining it concretely as the actual KERNEL_WATERMARK constant, but resolving cross-crate constants in Verus is genuinely difficult, and since check_user_watermark is external_body anyway, the abstraction is acceptable. I'll flag this as a quality concern but not a hard blocker, since uninterp isn't in the explicit guardrail blockers list.

Now I'm examining whether the watermark postcondition is actually the right thing — the policy should guarantee that after servicing an allocation, at least KERNEL_WATERMARK frames remain free, which is what the postcondition claims, but I need to verify this captures the intent correctly.

For kernel allocations, there's no watermark postcondition, which is correct since the kernel bypasses that policy.

There's a real gap in the user frame allocation spec: it doesn't guarantee the allocated frames are distinct. The spec allows `allocated_frames` to contain the same frame multiple times as long as the length matches the count, which means a buggy implementation could return count copies of a single frame and still satisfy the postcondition. The kernel bulk allocation avoids this because the contiguity requirement (each frame at base + i*PAGE_SIZE) mathematically implies distinctness, but the user bulk allocation has neither contiguity nor an explicit distinctness clause. This is a meaningful completeness issue — the spec should reject implementations that hand out duplicates.

There's also no mention of refcounts in the allocation specs. The design docs emphasize that freshly allocated user frames should have refcount 1 for copy-on-write semantics, but the actual postconditions only check that frames are in `allocated_frames`, not that their refcounts are set correctly.  The `wf()` invariant does guarantee allocated frames have positive refcounts, but not specifically 1, which is weaker than what the caller needs for exclusive ownership. That's another Medium-severity gap.

Stepping back to the pass/fail question: there are no hard blockers—no admission/assumption violations, all external functions are in the TCB list, AST matches, and verification succeeds. But there are several spec-completeness issues: the tautological error handlers, the near-vacuous init contract, and the missing distinctness guarantee on `alloc_many_user_frames` that would allow a buggy implementation to return duplicate frames.

The strict mandate requires zero blockers AND every quality criterion met. The distinctness gap is the most critical—it's exactly the kind of spec weakness that should catch bugs, yet the current spec admits a clearly-buggy implementation. That's a genuine failure of the specification's purpose. Even though some gaps (like error state preservation) are architectural limitations, the distinctness and refcount issues are expressible and should be captured. The spec doesn't actually guarantee that allocated frames are fresh or exclusive—a frame already owned by someone else would still satisfy the `allocated_frames.contains` check. This is a substantial gap from the design intent, which required exclusive ownership and a clean free→allocated transition. So I'm leaning toward FAIL on quality grounds: while there are no hard blockers (verification passes, no admits, TCB-compliant), the spec fails multiple completeness criteria—missing distinctness, freshness, exclusivity guarantees that the caller needs. The monotone carrier justifies *why* these are hard to capture, but doesn't make them complete. I should write the review objectively noting these gaps while acknowledging the design rationale.

Now I need to tally caller coverage: checking whether the spec actually ensures the success and failure paths that callers expect. For `init`, the spec captures that the singleton is established and `phys_view().initialized` holds, but it doesn't formally model the manager-singleton lifecycle or guarantee that `get_mut` will succeed afterward—that's only implicit. And for the error case, the spec says nothing about when `Err` is returned.

For `alloc_user_frame`, the success path covers watermark gating and allocation tracking, but doesn't capture the exclusivity guarantee (refcount 1). The error case just says `Err(_) => true`, which is vacuous.

In `alloc_many_user_frames`, the precondition covers vector emptiness but not the capacity check (that's handled at runtime). The success path confirms count and watermark but misses the no-double-allocation property. The error case covers vector cleanup but not the "no leak" or "state unchanged" guarantees.

For `alloc_kernel_frame`, I'm checking the same pattern—what's formally ensured versus what callers actually need. Tallying up the coverage across all six public functions and their success/failure paths: I've got six fully covered expectations, three that are only partially covered, and five that aren't covered at all—mostly the error cases that reduce to tautologies and the lifecycle initialization that isn't modeled in the spec.

For the caller-facing contracts, all six functions have documented expectations, but the success-path guarantees have some gaps like missing distinctness and refcount handling, while the failure paths are largely weak—four of the six functions essentially just return `true` for errors or don't characterize them at all, with only the bulk allocators capturing meaningful failure semantics around vector cleanup.

Reconciling against the bug report: I haven't found any actual code bugs—the implementation handles watermark overflow correctly with checked arithmetic and maintains proper all-or-nothing cleanup—but the gaps I'm seeing are specification gaps rather than code defects, which aligns with how bugs are classified here.

The notes in bugs.md about Verus front-end limitations for static mut and error macros are consistent with what's documented in tcb-allowed, so that's fine. I've also verified that the success ensures for alloc_user_frame include page alignment, and the watermark postcondition correctly guarantees the free space stays above the threshold. The assume_init_mut at line 147 isn't a verification concern since it's a standard library method in exec code, not a verification assume. I've confirmed there are no hidden admits or assumes in the included specs.

Now I'm ready to write up the review.

arguments.file_text:
# Final Independent Review — `mm::phys::manager` (`PhysMemoryManager`)

**Reviewer:** Independent strict final review (Claude)
**Date:** 2026-06-15
**Branch:** `verus-ai/phys-manager`  •  **HEAD:** `759a6857f`  •  **Pre-verus base:** `2cccace54` (`caller-analysis START`)
**Module:** `kernel::mm::phys` (target file `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs`)
**In-scope functions:** `init`, `alloc_user_frame`, `check_user_watermark`, `alloc_many_user_frames`, `alloc_many_kernel_frames`, `alloc_kernel_frame`

> **Headline:** No *hard* blockers — verification passes (exit 0, 0 errors), `admit=0`, `assume=0`,
> all 6 `external_body` shims are pre-approved in `tcb-allowed.md`, AST is byte-for-byte consistent,
> and no spec was weakened. **However**, the realized contracts have several genuine
> **spec-completeness gaps** that fail the strict quality bar: tautological `Err(_) => true` arms,
> an effectively vacuous `init` contract, a missing **no-double-allocation/distinctness** guarantee on
> the user bulk path (the spec admits a buggy implementation), missing fresh-ownership (refcount=1)
> facts, and a `uninterp` watermark spec fn that `verus-constraints` bans. **Final Result: FAIL on
> quality grounds.**

---

## 0. Evidence Index (commands run)

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Verification | `make verify-kernel MODULE=mm::phys` | exit 0, 0 errors (cached) |
| AST consistency | `ast_consistency.py --base-ref 2cccace54 manager.rs count/summary` | ✅ 7 fns + 1 struct MATCH |
| Fn coverage | `fn_coverage.py manager.orig.rs manager.rs` | 7/7 matched, 0 missing, 0 extra |
| Spec drift (instructed) | `spec_drift.py git-diff manager.rs --before HEAD` | exit 0 — no drift |
| Spec drift (vs base) | `spec_drift.py git-diff manager.rs --before 2cccace54` | exit 1 — only *additions* (new contracts), 0 ensures removed |
| `VERUS REWRITE` scan | `grep -rn "VERUS REWRITE\|DEVIATION\|BUG FIX"` | none |
| Cheating grep | per-file `grep` of admit/assume/external_body/cfg | see §7 |

---

## 1. Spec Quality (external-top API contracts)

The six methods are `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` shims with `#[verus_spec]` contracts stated over
the do-not-modify `phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView`. Because the carrier is the **global** `phys_view()`
with **no `old(phys_view())` handle** (per `view_design.md`), contracts are *monotone post-state facts*.
This is an acknowledged, pre-approved architectural choice — but it does not exempt the contracts from
the spec-design quality bar, and several clauses fall short.

### 1.1 Tautological error postconditions — `Err(_) => true` (anti-pattern #5/#8)

Three functions specify nothing on the error path:

- `alloc_user_frame` — `manager.rs:264` → `Err(_) => true`
- `check_user_watermark` — `manager.rs:304` → `Err(_) => true`
- `alloc_kernel_frame` — `manager.rs:349` → `Err(_) => true`

`caller_analysis.md` (L73, L101–102, L127) states callers rely on the error path meaning **"nothing was
allocated; no frame leaks; allocator left untouched."** None of that is captured. The unconditional
`phys_view().inv()` + `phys_view().initialized` ensures (e.g. `manager.rs:255–256, 298–300, 342–343`)
*partially* mitigate (the allocator stays well-formed on error), but "no leak / state-preserved" is **not
formally guaranteed**. This is precisely spec-design Anti-Pattern #5 (One-Sided Error Spec) and #8
(Tautological Postcondition).

*Mitigation note:* with no `old(phys_view())`, state-preservation on a value-less `Err` is genuinely
inexpressible for the **single-frame** paths — `Err(_) => true` is the maximum achievable there. This is
a limitation of the pre-approved carrier, not laziness. It is still a real completeness gap that the
caller-required guarantee is not met.

### 1.2 `init` contract is effectively vacuous (missing the property the caller needs)

`init` (`manager.rs:99–106`): `requires phys_view().initialized, phys_view().inv()` and
`ensures phys_view().inv(), phys_view().initialized`. Since the postcondition merely **restates the
precondition**, the contract is a frame-preservation no-op. The caller-relevant effect that
`caller_analysis.md` (L53–61) names — *"after Ok, the singleton is established and every later
`get_mut()`/`alloc_*` is valid; one-shot/monotonic; second call errors"* — is **not captured**: the
manager-singleton `AtomicBool` lifecycle has no abstract model (`manager.rs:91–96`). The `Err`
(double-init) condition is entirely unspecified (the ensures are unconditional, no `match`). A caller
cannot prove from this spec that `get_mut()` will not panic after `init`. **Weak / incomplete.**

The precondition `phys_view().initialized` is *correct and satisfiable* (boot calls `frame::init` →
region booking → `Upool::new` **before** `PhysMemoryManager::init`, per `caller_analysis.md` L14–17), but
it means `init` proves nothing new.

### 1.3 Missing "no-double-allocation"/distinctness on the user bulk path (admits a buggy impl)

`alloc_many_user_frames` Ok arm (`manager.rs:187–194`):
```
final(frames)@.len() == count
forall|i| 0 <= i < count ==> allocated_frames.contains(final(frames)@[i]@)
free_frames.finite()
spec_watermark_ok(frames, 0)
```
`allocated_frames` is a `Set<int>`. **Nothing forbids the `count` returned frames from sharing the same
address.** A buggy implementation that pushes the *same* frame `count` times satisfies every clause
(`len==count`, the single address is `contains`-ed, watermark holds). Per spec-design quality test #3
("if you can imagine a buggy implementation that still satisfies the spec, the spec is incomplete"),
this contract is **insufficient to reject bugs**. `caller_analysis.md` L91 and the Key-Invariants
("no double-allocation", L146–147) explicitly require distinctness/exclusivity.

Contrast `alloc_many_kernel_frames`, whose `kernel_frames_contiguous(frames, base)`
(`manager.rs:403–404`) **does** imply pairwise-distinct addresses (proved by
`lemma_contiguous_run_distinct`, `manager.proof.rs:32–58`). The user bulk path has **no** such
distinctness clause — an asymmetric gap.

### 1.4 Missing freshness / exclusive-ownership (refcount = 1)

`view_design.md` (L133–148, §"Design Rationale") and `caller_analysis.md` (refcount rationale) intend
"freshly allocated ⇒ refcount 1" for user CoW. The realized success arms only assert
`allocated_frames.contains(frame@)` — never `refcounts[frame@] == 1`, and never that the frame was
**previously free** (`free_frames.contains(addr)` in `old`). Via `wf()` an allocated frame has *some*
refcount in `1..=255`, but not specifically `1`, and not "fresh". The exclusive-ownership guarantee the
CoW caller relies on (`vmem.rs:879`) is therefore weaker than designed. **Incomplete.**

### 1.5 What is done well

- **Watermark policy split is correct and surfaced.** User success arms ensure
  `spec_watermark_ok(phys_view().frames, 0)` (`manager.rs:193, 262`) — i.e. ≥ `KERNEL_WATERMARK` frames
  remain free *after* servicing. Kernel paths (`alloc_kernel_frame`, `alloc_many_kernel_frames`)
  correctly omit any watermark clause (`manager.rs:344–348, 397–405`). Matches `caller_analysis.md`
  L151–152.
- **Page alignment** asserted on single-frame allocs (`frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0`,
  `manager.rs:260, 347`).
- **Contiguity** for kernel stacks via `exists|base| kernel_frames_contiguous(...)`
  (`manager.rs:403–404`) — load-bearing and well-modeled, backed by a real distinctness lemma.
- **All-or-nothing vector rollback** captured on both bulk error arms via `final(frames)@.len() == 0`
  (`manager.rs:195, 406`).
- `match`-on-result form (not separate `is_ok()/is_err()`) is used throughout — complete by
  construction for the arms present.

**§1 verdict:** Contracts are well-structured and the success-path watermark/contiguity/alignment facts
are strong, but error-path rigor and the core ownership guarantees (distinctness, freshness, init
lifecycle) are missing. **Quality criterion NOT fully met.**

---

## 2. Caller Coverage (`caller_analysis.md`)

6 in-scope functions, success **and** failure expectations each. "Covered" = a `requires`/`ensures`
formally provides the caller-relied guarantee.

| # | Expectation (from caller_analysis) | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| init — Ok (singleton live, get_mut won't panic) | ❌ Missing | lifecycle unmodeled, `manager.rs:103–105` only restates precond |
| init — Err (only when already init) | ❌ Missing | no `match`/Err clause |
| alloc_user_frame — Ok (owned, watermarked, distinct) | ⚠ Partial | allocated+aligned+watermark ✅; exclusivity/refcount ❌ (`:258–263`) |
| alloc_user_frame — Err (no alloc, no leak) | ❌ Missing | `Err(_) => true` (`:264`) |
| alloc_many_user_frames — preconds (empty Vec) | ✅ Covered | `requires old(frames)@.len()==0` (`:182`); capacity via runtime Err |
| alloc_many_user_frames — Ok (exactly count, owned) | ⚠ Partial | len+allocated+watermark ✅; **distinctness ❌** (`:187–193`) |
| alloc_many_user_frames — Err (emptied, freed, no leak) | ⚠ Partial | vector emptied ✅ (`:195`); no-leak/state ❌ |
| alloc_kernel_frame — Ok (owned, watermark bypass) | ✅ Covered | allocated+aligned, no watermark (`:345–348`) (minus refcount) |
| alloc_kernel_frame — Err (no leak, raw freed) | ❌ Missing | `Err(_) => true` (`:349`) |
| alloc_many_kernel_frames — preconds (empty Vec) | ✅ Covered | `requires old(frames)@.len()==0` (`:393`) |
| alloc_many_kernel_frames — Ok (count, contiguous) | ✅ Covered | len+allocated+contiguity (`:398–405`) |

## 1. Spec Quality (external-top API contracts)

The six methods are `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` shims with `#[verus_spec]` contracts stated over
the do-not-modify `phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView`. Because the carrier is the **global** `phys_view()`
with **no `old(phys_view())` handle** (per `view_design.md`), contracts are *monotone post-state facts*.
This is an acknowledged, pre-approved architectural choice — but it does not exempt the contracts from
the spec-design quality bar, and several clauses fall short.

### 1.1 Tautological error postconditions — `Err(_) => true` (anti-pattern #5/#8)

Three functions specify nothing on the error path:

- `alloc_user_frame` — `manager.rs:264` → `Err(_) => true`
- `check_user_watermark` — `manager.rs:304` → `Err(_) => true`
- `alloc_kernel_frame` — `manager.rs:349` → `Err(_) => true`

`caller_analysis.md` (L73, L101–102, L127) states callers rely on the error path meaning **"nothing was
allocated; no frame leaks; allocator left untouched."** None of that is captured. The unconditional
`phys_view().inv()` + `phys_view().initialized` ensures (e.g. `manager.rs:255–256, 298–300, 342–343`)
*partially* mitigate (the allocator stays well-formed on error), but "no leak / state-preserved" is **not
formally guaranteed**. This is precisely spec-design Anti-Pattern #5 (One-Sided Error Spec) and #8
(Tautological Postcondition).

*Mitigation note:* with no `old(phys_view())`, state-preservation on a value-less `Err` is genuinely
inexpressible for the **single-frame** paths — `Err(_) => true` is the maximum achievable there. This is
a limitation of the pre-approved carrier, not laziness. It is still a real completeness gap that the
caller-required guarantee is not met.

### 1.2 `init` contract is effectively vacuous (missing the property the caller needs)

`init` (`manager.rs:99–106`): `requires phys_view().initialized, phys_view().inv()` and
`ensures phys_view().inv(), phys_view().initialized`. Since the postcondition merely **restates the
precondition**, the contract is a frame-preservation no-op. The caller-relevant effect that
`caller_analysis.md` (L53–61) names — *"after Ok, the singleton is established and every later
`get_mut()`/`alloc_*` is valid; one-shot/monotonic; second call errors"* — is **not captured**: the
manager-singleton `AtomicBool` lifecycle has no abstract model (`manager.rs:91–96`). The `Err`
(double-init) condition is entirely unspecified (the ensures are unconditional, no `match`). A caller
cannot prove from this spec that `get_mut()` will not panic after `init`. **Weak / incomplete.**

The precondition `phys_view().initialized` is *correct and satisfiable* (boot calls `frame::init` →
region booking → `Upool::new` **before** `PhysMemoryManager::init`, per `caller_analysis.md` L14–17), but
it means `init` proves nothing new.

### 1.3 Missing "no-double-allocation"/distinctness on the user bulk path (admits a buggy impl)

`alloc_many_user_frames` Ok arm (`manager.rs:187–194`):
```
final(frames)@.len() == count
forall|i| 0 <= i < count ==> allocated_frames.contains(final(frames)@[i]@)
free_frames.finite()
spec_watermark_ok(frames, 0)
```
`allocated_frames` is a `Set<int>`. **Nothing forbids the `count` returned frames from sharing the same
address.** A buggy implementation that pushes the *same* frame `count` times satisfies every clause
(`len==count`, the single address is `contains`-ed, watermark holds). Per spec-design quality test #3
("if you can imagine a buggy implementation that still satisfies the spec, the spec is incomplete"),
this contract is **insufficient to reject bugs**. `caller_analysis.md` L91 and the Key-Invariants
("no double-allocation", L146–147) explicitly require distinctness/exclusivity.

Contrast `alloc_many_kernel_frames`, whose `kernel_frames_contiguous(frames, base)`
(`manager.rs:403–404`) **does** imply pairwise-distinct addresses (proved by
`lemma_contiguous_run_distinct`, `manager.proof.rs:32–58`). The user bulk path has **no** such
distinctness clause — an asymmetric gap.

### 1.4 Missing freshness / exclusive-ownership (refcount = 1)

`view_design.md` (L133–148, §"Design Rationale") and `caller_analysis.md` (refcount rationale) intend
"freshly allocated ⇒ refcount 1" for user CoW. The realized success arms only assert
`allocated_frames.contains(frame@)` — never `refcounts[frame@] == 1`, and never that the frame was
**previously free** (`free_frames.contains(addr)` in `old`). Via `wf()` an allocated frame has *some*
refcount in `1..=255`, but not specifically `1`, and not "fresh". The exclusive-ownership guarantee the
CoW caller relies on (`vmem.rs:879`) is therefore weaker than designed. **Incomplete.**

### 1.5 What is done well

- **Watermark policy split is correct and surfaced.** User success arms ensure
  `spec_watermark_ok(phys_view().frames, 0)` (`manager.rs:193, 262`) — i.e. ≥ `KERNEL_WATERMARK` frames
  remain free *after* servicing. Kernel paths (`alloc_kernel_frame`, `alloc_many_kernel_frames`)
  correctly omit any watermark clause (`manager.rs:344–348, 397–405`). Matches `caller_analysis.md`
  L151–152.
- **Page alignment** asserted on single-frame allocs (`frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0`,
  `manager.rs:260, 347`).
- **Contiguity** for kernel stacks via `exists|base| kernel_frames_contiguous(...)`
  (`manager.rs:403–404`) — load-bearing and well-modeled, backed by a real distinctness lemma.
- **All-or-nothing vector rollback** captured on both bulk error arms via `final(frames)@.len() == 0`
  (`manager.rs:195, 406`).
- `match`-on-result form (not separate `is_ok()/is_err()`) is used throughout — complete by
  construction for the arms present.

**§1 verdict:** Contracts are well-structured and the success-path watermark/contiguity/alignment facts
are strong, but error-path rigor and the core ownership guarantees (distinctness, freshness, init
lifecycle) are missing. **Quality criterion NOT fully met.**

## Final Result: **FAIL**

**Rationale.** There are **no hard blockers** — verification passes with zero errors, there are zero
`admit()`/`assume()`, every `external_body` is pre-approved in `tcb-allowed.md`, AST is byte-identical to
the baseline, and no existing spec was weakened. The proof artifacts are clean and the success-path

spec-design's core test of being *"sufficient to reject bugs."* Most critically, `alloc_many_user_frames`
admits an implementation that hands out `count` aliases of the same physical frame (H1), the three

+## 1. Spec Quality (external-top API contracts)
+
+The six methods are `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` shims with `#[verus_spec]` contracts stated over
+the do-not-modify `phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView`. Because the carrier is the **global** `phys_view()`
+with **no `old(phys_view())` handle** (per `view_design.md`), contracts are *monotone post-state facts*.
+This is an acknowledged, pre-approved architectural choice — but it does not exempt the contracts from
+the spec-design quality bar, and several clauses fall short.
+
+### 1.1 Tautological error postconditions — `Err(_) => true` (anti-pattern #5/#8)
+
+Three functions specify nothing on the error path:
+
+- `alloc_user_frame` — `manager.rs:264` → `Err(_) => true`
+- `check_user_watermark` — `manager.rs:304` → `Err(_) => true`
+- `alloc_kernel_frame` — `manager.rs:349` → `Err(_) => true`
+
+`caller_analysis.md` (L73, L101–102, L127) states callers rely on the error path meaning **"nothing was
+allocated; no frame leaks; allocator left untouched."** None of that is captured. The unconditional
+`phys_view().inv()` + `phys_view().initialized` ensures (e.g. `manager.rs:255–256, 298–300, 342–343`)
+*partially* mitigate (the allocator stays well-formed on error), but "no leak / state-preserved" is **not
+formally guaranteed**. This is precisely spec-design Anti-Pattern #5 (One-Sided Error Spec) and #8
+(Tautological Postcondition).
+
+*Mitigation note:* with no `old(phys_view())`, state-preservation on a value-less `Err` is genuinely
+inexpressible for the **single-frame** paths — `Err(_) => true` is the maximum achievable there. This is
+a limitation of the pre-approved carrier, not laziness. It is still a real completeness gap that the
+caller-required guarantee is not met.
+
+### 1.2 `init` contract is effectively vacuous (missing the property the caller needs)
+
+`init` (`manager.rs:99–106`): `requires phys_view().initialized, phys_view().inv()` and
+`ensures phys_view().inv(), phys_view().initialized`. Since the postcondition merely **restates the
+precondition**, the contract is a frame-preservation no-op. The caller-relevant effect that
+`caller_analysis.md` (L53–61) names — *"after Ok, the singleton is established and every later
+`get_mut()`/`alloc_*` is valid; one-shot/monotonic; second call errors"* — is **not captured**: the
+manager-singleton `AtomicBool` lifecycle has no abstract model (`manager.rs:91–96`). The `Err`
+(double-init) condition is entirely unspecified (the ensures are unconditional, no `match`). A caller
+cannot prove from this spec that `get_mut()` will not panic after `init`. **Weak / incomplete.**
+
+The precondition `phys_view().initialized` is *correct and satisfiable* (boot calls `frame::init` →
+region booking → `Upool::new` **before** `PhysMemoryManager::init`, per `caller_analysis.md` L14–17), but
+it means `init` proves nothing new.
+
+### 1.3 Missing "no-double-allocation"/distinctness on the user bulk path (admits a buggy impl)
+
+`alloc_many_user_frames` Ok arm (`manager.rs:187–194`):
+```
+final(frames)@.len() == count
+forall|i| 0 <= i < count ==> allocated_frames.contains(final(frames)@[i]@)
+free_frames.finite()
+spec_watermark_ok(frames, 0)
+```
+`allocated_frames` is a `Set<int>`. **Nothing forbids the `count` returned frames from sharing the same
+address.** A buggy implementation that pushes the *same* frame `count` times satisfies every clause
+(`len==count`, the single address is `contains`-ed, watermark holds). Per spec-design quality test #3
+("if you can imagine a buggy implementation that still satisfies the spec, the spec is incomplete"),
+this contract is **insufficient to reject bugs**. `caller_analysis.md` L91 and the Key-Invariants
+("no double-allocation", L146–147) explicitly require distinctness/exclusivity.
+
+Contrast `alloc_many_kernel_frames`, whose `kernel_frames_contiguous(frames, base)`
+(`manager.rs:403–404`) **does** imply pairwise-distinct addresses (proved by
+`lemma_contiguous_run_distinct`, `manager.proof.rs:32–58`). The user bulk path has **no** such
+distinctness clause — an asymmetric gap.
+
+### 1.4 Missing freshness / exclusive-ownership (refcount = 1)
+
+`view_design.md` (L133–148, §"Design Rationale") and `caller_analysis.md` (refcount rationale) intend
+"freshly allocated ⇒ refcount 1" for user CoW. The realized success arms only assert
+`allocated_frames.contains(frame@)` — never `refcounts[frame@] == 1`, and never that the frame was
+**previously free** (`free_frames.contains(addr)` in `old`). Via `wf()` an allocated frame has *some*
+refcount in `1..=255`, but not specifically `1`, and not "fresh". The exclusive-ownership guarantee the
+CoW caller relies on (`vmem.rs:879`) is therefore weaker than designed. **Incomplete.**
+
+### 1.5 What is done well
+
+- **Watermark policy split is correct and surfaced.** User success arms ensure
+  `spec_watermark_ok(phys_view().frames, 0)` (`manager.rs:193, 262`) — i.e. ≥ `KERNEL_WATERMARK` frames
+  remain free *after* servicing. Kernel paths (`alloc_kernel_frame`, `alloc_many_kernel_frames`)
+  correctly omit any watermark clause (`manager.rs:344–348, 397–405`). Matches `caller_analysis.md`
+  L151–152.
+- **Page alignment** asserted on single-frame allocs (`frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0`,
+  `manager.rs:260, 347`).
+- **Contiguity** for kernel stacks via `exists|base| kernel_frames_contiguous(...)`
+  (`manager.rs:403–404`) — load-bearing and well-modeled, backed by a real distinctness lemma.
+- **All-or-nothing vector rollback** captured on both bulk error arms via `final(frames)@.len() == 0`
+  (`manager.rs:195, 406`).
+- `match`-on-result form (not separate `is_ok()/is_err()`) is used throughout — complete by
+  construction for the arms present.
+
+**§1 verdict:** Contracts are well-structured and the success-path watermark/contiguity/alignment facts
+are strong, but error-path rigor and the core ownership guarantees (distinctness, freshness, init
+lifecycle) are missing. **Quality criterion NOT fully met.**

 **Reviewer:** Independent strict final review (Claude)
 **Date:** 2026-06-15
 **Branch:** `verus-ai/phys-manager`  •  **HEAD:** `759a6857f`  •  **Pre-verus base:** `2cccace54` (`caller-analysis START`)
 **Module:** `kernel::mm::phys` (target file `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs`)
 **In-scope functions:** `init`, `alloc_user_frame`, `check_user_watermark`, `alloc_many_user_frames`, `alloc_many_kernel_frames`, `alloc_kernel_frame`
 
 > **Headline:** No *hard* blockers — verification passes (exit 0, 0 errors), `admit=0`, `assume=0`,
 > all 6 `external_body` shims are pre-approved in `tcb-allowed.md`, AST is byte-for-byte consistent,
 > and no spec was weakened. **However**, the realized contracts have several genuine
 > **spec-completeness gaps** that fail the strict quality bar: tautological `Err(_) => true` arms,
 > an effectively vacuous `init` contract, a missing **no-double-allocation/distinctness** guarantee on
 > the user bulk path (the spec admits a buggy implementation), missing fresh-ownership (refcount=1)
 > facts, and a `uninterp` watermark spec fn that `verus-constraints` bans. **Final Result: FAIL on
 > quality grounds.**

 | Check | Command | Result |

 ## 1. Spec Quality (external-top API contracts)
 
 The six methods are `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` shims with `#[verus_spec]` contracts stated over
 the do-not-modify `phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView`. Because the carrier is the **global** `phys_view()`
 with **no `old(phys_view())` handle** (per `view_design.md`), contracts are *monotone post-state facts*.
 This is an acknowledged, pre-approved architectural choice — but it does not exempt the contracts from
 the spec-design quality bar, and several clauses fall short.
 
 ### 1.1 Tautological error postconditions — `Err(_) => true` (anti-pattern #5/#8)
 
 Three functions specify nothing on the error path:
 
 - `alloc_user_frame` — `manager.rs:264` → `Err(_) => true`
 - `check_user_watermark` — `manager.rs:304` → `Err(_) => true`
 - `alloc_kernel_frame` — `manager.rs:349` → `Err(_) => true`
 
 `caller_analysis.md` (L73, L101–102, L127) states callers rely on the error path meaning **"nothing was
 allocated; no frame leaks; allocator left untouched."** None of that is captured. The unconditional
 `phys_view().inv()` + `phys_view().initialized` ensures (e.g. `manager.rs:255–256, 298–300, 342–343`)
 *partially* mitigate (the allocator stays well-formed on error), but "no leak / state-preserved" is **not
 formally guaranteed**. This is precisely spec-design Anti-Pattern #5 (One-Sided Error Spec) and #8
 (Tautological Postcondition).
 
 *Mitigation note:* with no `old(phys_view())`, state-preservation on a value-less `Err` is genuinely
 inexpressible for the **single-frame** paths — `Err(_) => true` is the maximum achievable there. This is
 a limitation of the pre-approved carrier, not laziness. It is still a real completeness gap that the
 caller-required guarantee is not met.
 
 ### 1.2 `init` contract is effectively vacuous (missing the property the caller needs)
 
 `init` (`manager.rs:99–106`): `requires phys_view().initialized, phys_view().inv()` and
 `ensures phys_view().inv(), phys_view().initialized`. Since the postcondition merely **restates the
 precondition**, the contract is a frame-preservation no-op. The caller-relevant effect that
 `caller_analysis.md` (L53–61) names — *"after Ok, the singleton is established and every later
 `get_mut()`/`alloc_*` is valid; one-shot/monotonic; second call errors"* — is **not captured**: the
 manager-singleton `AtomicBool` lifecycle has no abstract model (`manager.rs:91–96`). The `Err`
 (double-init) condition is entirely unspecified (the ensures are unconditional, no `match`). A caller
 cannot prove from this spec that `get_mut()` will not panic after `init`. **Weak / incomplete.**
 
 The precondition `phys_view().initialized` is *correct and satisfiable* (boot calls `frame::init` →
 region booking → `Upool::new` **before** `PhysMemoryManager::init`, per `caller_analysis.md` L14–17), but
 it means `init` proves nothing new.

# Final Comprehensive Review: phys-manager

**Module:** `kernel::mm::phys` • **Target file:** `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs`
**Branch:** `verus-ai/phys-manager` • **Date:** 2026-06-15
**Method:** two independent sub-agent reviews (one per allowed model) reconciled below.
- `final_review.claude.md` — model `claude-opus-4.8`
- `final_review.codex.md` — model `gpt-5.3-codex`

Both reviewers independently reached **FAIL**: all *mechanical* gates pass (verification,
admit/assume, TCB, AST, spec-drift), but the realized contracts miss several **spec-design /
verus-constraints quality criteria** (tautological error arms, a vacuous `init` contract, a missing
distinctness guarantee on the user bulk path, and a banned `uninterp` watermark spec fn).

### Caller Analysis
- [x] All pub functions have callers searched (tool-verified, not manual claim)
- [x] Caller expectations (success + failure) documented for each pub function
- [x] Abstract resource identified (global frame-reservation state via `phys_view()`/`FrameAllocView`)
- [x] Pre-existing specs assessed (do-not-modify `FrameAllocView`/`Inner` views from upstream)

- [x] All caller-observable state represented (no missing fields)
- [x] No implementation-specific fields (only caller-observable state)

- [x] Mathematical types used (int/Seq/Set/Map; addresses keep usize)

### Specification
- [x] Every in-scope exec function has requires/ensures (`fn_coverage.py` → 7/7 matched)
- [ ] Caller coverage: each caller expectation has corresponding requires/ensures — **FAIL** (success paths strong; multiple failure-path + lifecycle expectations missing — see Caller Coverage)
- [x] View consistency: specs reference `FrameAllocView` fields and maintain `inv()`
- [ ] No tautological ensures — **FAIL**: `Err(_) => true` on `alloc_user_frame` (`:264`), `check_user_watermark` (`:303`), `alloc_kernel_frame` (`:349`) (anti-pattern #8)
- [ ] No subsumed ensures — **FAIL**: `init` ensures (`:104–105`) merely restate its `requires` (`:101–102`); contract is a vacuous no-op
- [ ] Error paths have meaningful ensures — **FAIL**: three `Err(_) => true` arms (anti-pattern #5, One-Sided Error); bulk Err arms give only `len==0`, not "no-leak"
- [x] No assume_specification for workspace-internal code (0 in module)
- [x] vstd searched before any assume_specification (none used)
- [x] Specs written for the caller (success-path facts are caller-usable)
- [x] Trait obligations satisfied (no trait impls in scope beyond derives)
- [ ] Spec completeness (advisory) — **GAPS**: missing distinctness/no-double-alloc (H1) and fresh-ownership/refcount=1 (M2)
- [x] Loop invariants — N/A (all six bodies are `external_body`; no verified loops in scope)

- [x] Exec rewrites minimal/equivalent — N/A, **zero** `// VERUS REWRITE` in module
- [x] Cross-module regression (module verify PASS; kernel::all PASS at HEAD)

- [x] Cross-module regression (module verify PASS)
- [ ] Verification: `make verify-kernel` + `make build` — 0 errors, 0 warnings — build not re-run — **partial**

### Bug Recording
- [x] bugs.md exists; correctly records "None"
- [x] Each (n/a) bug would be a real defect — none found
- [x] Bug entry format — n/a (no bugs)
- [x] No external_body used to mask a code defect (shims justified by genuine Verus limits)
- [x] Bug entries include provenance — n/a

## Spec Quality
The six methods are `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` shims with `#[verus_spec]` contracts over the
do-not-modify `phys_view()`/`FrameAllocView`. Because the carrier is the global `phys_view()` with **no
`old(phys_view())`**, contracts are monotone post-state facts (a pre-approved architectural choice).
**Success-path facts are good and caller-usable** (allocated-membership + page alignment for single
allocs; exact `count` + per-frame membership + watermark for bulk user; exact `count` + contiguity for
bulk kernel — `kernel_frames_contiguous`). The supporting lemmas (`lemma_watermark_monotone`,
`lemma_contiguous_run_distinct`) are fully discharged (no admit/assume).

**Quality deficiencies (why both reviewers FAIL it):**
- **Tautological error arms** `Err(_) => true` on `alloc_user_frame`, `check_user_watermark`,
  `alloc_kernel_frame` (anti-patterns #5/#8). Callers expect "nothing allocated / allocator untouched";
  not captured. (For value-less single-frame `Err` with no `old(phys_view())`, this is partly inherent
  to the carrier, but the guarantee is still absent.)
- **`init` contract is vacuous** — ensures (`:104–105`) restate requires (`:101–102`); the singleton
  lifecycle / double-init `Err` semantics callers rely on (`caller_analysis.md` L53–61) are unmodeled.
- **Missing distinctness on the user bulk path** — `alloc_many_user_frames` Ok arm (`:188–193`) has no
  no-double-allocation clause; the spec is satisfiable by an impl returning `count` aliases of one frame
  (kernel bulk path is fine via contiguity).
- **`spec_kernel_watermark()` is `uninterp`** (`manager.spec.rs:35`) — explicitly **banned** by
  verus-constraints (line 113) and spec-design anti-pattern #12; it is a standalone spec fn, not a
  `View::view()` of an external_body type, so the exception does not apply.
- **Missing fresh-ownership** (`refcount==1`, `addr ∈ old free_frames`) on all alloc success arms.
- **Bulk Err arms** capture only `final(frames)@.len()==0`, not allocator no-leak/rollback.

Reviewers differ in strictness on the count; consensus: **success paths well covered, failure +
lifecycle paths weak.**
- Claude: **6/14 fully covered**, 4 partial, 4 missing.
- Codex: **3/14 fully covered**, 6 partial, 5 missing.
- Consolidated **Covered: 6 / 14** (best case), **Total: 14**.
- Missing / partial (union):
  - `init` success lifecycle guarantee (singleton established for later `get_mut`) — **missing**
  - `init` error condition (already-initialized → InvalidArgument) — **missing**
  - `alloc_user_frame` failure "no allocation / no leak" — **missing** (`Err(_)=>true`)
  - `alloc_kernel_frame` failure "no leak" incl. wrap-failure path — **missing** (`Err(_)=>true`)
  - `check_user_watermark` error classification (overflow vs breach) + converse `Err => !policy` — **missing**
  - `alloc_user_frame` / `alloc_kernel_frame` fresh/exclusive ownership (refcount=1) — **partial**
  - `alloc_many_*` capacity-check / InvalidArgument failure behavior — **partial**
  - `alloc_many_*` failure all-or-nothing **no-leak** (beyond `len==0`) — **partial**
  - `alloc_many_user_frames` success **distinctness** — **missing** (admits aliasing impl)

- Remaining admit(): **0** — none. (no BLOCKER)
- Remaining external_body not in `tcb-allowed.md`: **0** — all 6 (`manager.rs:107,198,267,306,352,409`)
  are listed in the pre-approved TCB. (no BLOCKER)

## TCB Compliance
- All external_body listed in `tcb-allowed.md`: **YES**. The six `PhysMemoryManager` methods are
  enumerated in the "Allowed `external_body` — `PhysMemoryManager`" section. No unapproved trust
  boundary introduced.

## Guardrails Compliance
(counts over `manager.rs`, `manager.spec.rs`, `manager.proof.rs`)
- admit: **0**, assume: **0**, external_body: **6** (all pre-approved; `:98,177,249,292,336,388`),
  assume_specification: **0**, cfg-gated exec: **0** (only `#[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)] include!` at
  `:9,11` and `cfg_attr(... allow ...)` at `:97,291` — not exec-logic forks).

## AST Consistency
- AST check: **PASS** — `ast_consistency.py` → matched=7 fns + 1 struct, mismatched=0, missing=0,
  extra=0. Zero `// VERUS REWRITE` comments in the module (no exec rewrites to audit).

## Verification
- verus: **PASS** — `make verify-kernel MODULE=mm::phys` exit 0, **0 errors** (canonical run + both
  sub-agents independently confirmed). `kernel::all` reported passing at branch HEAD (git log).

## Bug Summary
- Total bugs recorded: **0** (`bugs.md` = "None", reconciled accurate).
- True Bugs: **0**. Cleanup/rollback paths are leak-free; the six shims are justified by genuine Verus
  front-end limitations (no `static mut` model; `error!`/`warn!` macros unsupported), not by masking a
  defect. No new code defects discovered during this review — all new findings are
  spec-completeness/quality issues, correctly **not** logged as bugs.

## Issues (highest priority first)
1. **[BLOCKER — verus-constraints]** `spec_kernel_watermark()` is `uninterp` (`manager.spec.rs:35`).
   `uninterp spec fn` is banned (verus-constraints L113; spec-design #12). Must be given a concrete
   definition (e.g. tied to `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`) — it is not a `View::view()` exception.
2. **[Quality]** Tautological `Err(_) => true` on `alloc_user_frame` (`:264`), `check_user_watermark`
   (`:303`), `alloc_kernel_frame` (`:349`) — anti-patterns #5/#8; add meaningful failure guarantees.
3. **[Quality]** `init` contract vacuous (`:101–106`) — restates precondition; does not model the
   singleton lifecycle / double-init `Err` callers depend on.
4. **[Quality]** `alloc_many_user_frames` Ok arm (`:188–193`) lacks distinctness/no-double-allocation —
   spec admits an aliasing implementation.
5. **[Quality]** Missing fresh-ownership (`refcount==1`, drawn from old free set) on all alloc success
   arms; bulk Err arms capture only `len==0`, not allocator no-leak.
6. **[Coverage]** Failure-path + lifecycle caller expectations largely uncovered (see Caller Coverage).

## Result: **FAIL**

All mechanical/cheating gates pass (verification 0 errors; admit=0; assume=0; external_body=6 all in the
pre-approved TCB; AST consistent; no spec weakening; no bugs), so there are **no hard cheating/TCB/AST
blockers**. However, the strict bar requires **every** checklist item checked, and multiple
specification-quality and caller-coverage items are unmet — most critically the **banned `uninterp`
watermark spec fn** (a direct verus-constraints violation), the **tautological `Err(_) => true`** error
arms, the **vacuous `init` contract**, and the **missing distinctness** guarantee on the user bulk path.
Per "PASS only if ALL checklist items are checked," the verdict is **FAIL**.
